articles.title: World Series Winners: Complete list of champions by year
articles.summary: See every World Series winner from 1903 to 2026, including the Milwaukee Brewers' first title in 2026, plus which teams have won the most championships
articles.body: The World Series is the ultimate culmination of every Major League Baseball season. It's played between the playoff finalist from the American League and the National League, and has taken place every year since 1903. Over the years, several teams have become MLB champions by winning multiple World Series titles. The New York Yankees hold the record with 27 championships, while the St. Louis Cardinals have won 11 and the Boston Red Sox have won nine. Other teams like the San Francisco Giants, Los Angeles Dodgers, and the Athletics have also made their mark with many championships. Throughout World Series history, there have been many unforgettable moments, like Bill Mazeroski's walk-off home run in 1960 that led the Pittsburgh Pirates to victory. And who could forget when the Boston Red Sox broke the "Curse of the Bambino" in 2004, finally winning their first championship in 86 years! In 2026, the Milwaukee Brewers won the first World Series title in franchise history, beating the Tampa Bay Rays four games to one. Milwaukee clinched with a 4-1 win in Game 5 on Oct. 28 at Tropicana Field, and catcher William Contreras was named World Series MVP. The year before, the Los Angeles Dodgers repeated as champions by beating the Toronto Blue Jays in a seven-game thriller. Despite the many changes that baseball has undergone over the years, the thrill of winning the World Series remains the same. Teams strive to become the best and etch their names in MLB history as World Series Winners. articles.title: La faceta deportiva del discutido Óscar Puente: "Lo paso fatal"
articles.standfirst: El ministro de Transportes, que gestiona el accidente ferroviario de Urda, es hincha del Valladolid (muy crítico con los árbitros) y ha practicado entre otros waterpolo, beisbol o golf
articles.summary: El ministro de Transportes, que gestiona ahora las consecuencias de la DANA, es hincha del Valladolid (muy crítico con los árbitros) y ha practicado entre otros waterpolo, beisbol o golf
articles.body: Azote de la oposición como se le considera (o consideraba), también lo ha sido y lo sigue siendo de los árbitros y del VAR. Porque Óscar Puente Santiago, discutido ahora por su gestión del sistema ferroviario, es entre otras cosas un hincha acérrimo del Valladolid. Y sus críticas a las actuaciones de los colegiados, además de propiciar algún sonoro encontronazo con el periodismo deportivo, se han dirigido también por elevación hacia la Federación Española ("Dejad de reclamar a Tebas. Los arbitrajes NO dependen de LaLiga, lo cual es sencillamente aberrante. Dependen de un ente del que si digo lo que pienso me cierran la cuenta"), hacia el Barcelona a cuenta de los pagos a Negreira ("7 MILLONES. Luego cuando los humildes nos quejamos de los arbitrajes es que vemos visiones") o hacia el Real Madrid ("En este país sólo pueden protestar al árbitro, incluso apechugarlo en grupos, o llamarle loco a la cara sin consecuencias, sus jugadores. Los demás oír ver y callar"). Puente, vallisoletano de 57 años, es ministro de Transportes y Movilidad Sostenible desde hace tres, además de haber sido alcalde de su ciudad durante dos legislaturas (perdió el bastón de mando a pesar de haber sido el más votado... y ése, el de encontrarse en parecidas condiciones que el líder popular, fue precisamente uno de los motivos por los que Pedro Sánchez le encomendó la réplica, que resultó durísima, al fallido discurso de investidura de Alberto Núñez Feijóo en septiembre de 2023). Pero además esconde una faceta personal deportiva que pasa por el fútbol, faltaría más, pero también por muchos otros: "Jugué dos años waterpolo en el Instituto Zorrilla, balonmano, baloncesto en Segunda División en La Salle Iberduero, beisbol en Estados Unidos, esquí, golf...", enumeraba hace años. Su hándicap en los 18 hoyos es 10,4, por cierto. Sin problema para fotografiarse luciendo camiseta o bufanda blanquivioletas, con familiares en el organigrama del club ("hablamos mucho de fútbol cuando nos reunimos y luego en el campo lo paso fatal"), el político también ha mantenido agrias polémicas con Ronaldo Nazario, al que recibió con los mejores deseos cuando se convirtió en máximo accionista, pero del que se fue distanciando con el paso del tiempo y al que dirigió varias de sus 'perlas'. "Yo no ficho, ni entreno ni salgo a jugar; yo no tengo responsabilidad en la marcha deportiva del club", dijo el entonces regidor. "No sabe ni en el país ni en la ciudad en la que vive [...] Ni yo le puedo regalar el estadio ni puedo cedérselo 50 años asumiendo los costes de las reformas que se hagan, no es posible en nuestro ordenamiento jurídico [...] Estas declaraciones son una cortina de humo sobre sus responsabilidades", apuntó cuando ya sabía que no iba a continuar en el puesto. Y es que el peso de la entidad para toda la capital resulta evidente en su opinión: "El Real Valladolid ha ayudado a muchos deportes, por ejemplo al rugby. No sólo se trata de fútbol. Es un buque insignia que tira de todo". De ahí la importancia que tendría su regreso a la máxima categoría, una vez que se ha convertido en los últimos tiempo en equipo 'ascensor' por excelencia. "Ahí has tirado con bala", espetó Puente en su día a Gemma Nierga, cuestionado sobre si veía más probable aprobar los Presupuestos Generales del Estado o que el Pucela se quedara en Primera. "Tiene una papeleta muy complicada. De hecho no hay ni lateral izquierdo. Pero no entremos ahí..." El político también ha tenido oportunidad de exhibir su destreza con el esférico, al menos cuando, en la Plaza Mayor de la ciudad y en el arranque de 2018, lanzó al portero Jordi Masip el primer penalti solidario de una acción que pretendía recaudar fondos para la investigación de la leucemia infantil. Pero es en la cancha de basket del Polideportivo Pisuerga donde Puente ha exhibido mejores fundamentos durante los partidos de exhibición que ha ido jugando en los últimos años. Incluso disputó un partido de baloncesto en silla de ruedas para, con motivo del Día Internacional de la Discapacidad, visibilidad la necesidad de avanzar en el ámbito de la inclusión. Era alcalde, por cierto, cuando los grandes clubes de Valladolid en ambos deportes alcanzaron un acuerdo de colaboración. También cambió el traje y la corbata por la ropa deportiva cuando, acompañado por otros miembros de la corporación municipal, inauguró la nueva pista de atletismo del Complejo Deportivo de Fuente la Mora (en ese caso aprovechó para apoyar la lucha contra la esclerosis múltiple). Por lo demás, otro de los cargos que ocupó en su día fue el de presidente de la Red Española de Ciudades Saludables, dedicado a proteger el bienestar de sus habitantes, y otra de las iniciativas que adoptó en su día fue la de utilizar la bicicleta para los desplazamientos cortos: "No es postureo, es una convicción de que estamos ante un medio de transporte rápido, limpio, sano y económico". Por entonces no podría imaginar que precisamente un día sería ministro del ramo y que suya sería la gestión de aeropuertos, puertos, carreteras... y vías. El deporte también estuvo en el origen de una anécdota que se remonta a finales de 2017, cuando, con motivo de un partido entre la Cultural y el Valladolid, se reunió con su homólogo de León y ambos posaron con las camisetas de sus respectivas escuadras. El problema es que una estaba patrocinada por la academia qatarí Aspire y la otra por la bodega Cuatro Rayas, lo que daba lugar a un mensaje equívoco cuando se juntaban. A vueltas con las drogas, una de las polémicas protagonizadas por Puente se originó tras acusar a Javier Milei, presidente de Argentina, de "ingesta de sustancias". La respuesta del dirigente sudamericano pasó por un comunicado en el que aludía a los "problemas más importante de los que ocuparse" que, según él, tenía Pedro Sánchez. Esa versión desatada del ministro español dio momentáneamente paso a otra cuando se desató aquella Dana que tantos daños humanos y materiales provocó. "Soy una persona tremendamente beligerante en términos políticos, pero me he propuesto centrarme en lo que necesita Valencia. Los políticos tenemos que hacer una llamada a la coordinación. Aparquemos la confrontación y dediquémonos exclusivamente a lo que la gente necesita", resumía al respecto. Dos años después, dos accidentes de tren después (en pocos meses, en el mismo trayecto y con numerosas víctimas mortales ambos), nadie se atreve a poner la mano en el fuego por que el ministro vaya a mantener su cargo. Óscar Puente, el deportista que dejó de serlo después de unas cuantas lesiones ("físicamente estoy muy mal"). Óscar Puente, el hincha.

articles.title: El 11% que separa a Antonelli de la eternidad
articles.standfirst: El piloto italiano deberá quedar entre los nueve primeros clasificados en el GP de México para proclamarse campeón a falta de dos grandes premios
articles.summary: El piloto italiano deberá quedar entre los nueve primeros clasificados en el GP de México para proclamarse campeón a falta de dos grandes premios
articles.body: La temporada de Fórmula 1 va llegando a su fin y Kimi Antonelli sigue descontando carreras para proclamarse campeón del mundo con apenas 20 años. El piloto de Mercedes tiene ante sí una oportunidad de oro para dejar el título resuelto en el Gran Premio de México y convertirse en el campeón más joven en la historia de la categoría. La cuenta atrás ha comenzado y el italiano está a un paso de culminar una temporada que puede marcar un antes y un después en su carrera. Antonelli ya tuvo la oportunidad de coronarse el pasado fin de semana en Austin. Hizo los deberes al cruzar la meta en primera posición, pero no dependía únicamente de su rendimiento: también necesitaba que Lewis Hamilton y su compañero George Russell no lograran los resultados necesarios para mantener viva la lucha por el campeonato. Ambos resistieron y aplazaron la celebración del italiano, que tendrá una nueva ocasión para cerrar el Mundial en México. Esta vez, el objetivo está mucho más cerca. De hecho, Antonelli ya depende exclusivamente de sí mismo para proclamarse campeón. Le bastará con terminar entre los nueve primeros clasificados en el circuito mexicano para asegurarse el título a falta de las dos últimas carreras de la temporada. Un escenario muy favorable si se tiene en cuenta su rendimiento durante el curso: en las 18 pruebas disputadas hasta ahora, solo se ha quedado fuera de ese grupo en dos ocasiones. Es decir, apenas algo más del 11% de las carreras. Un porcentaje que mantiene abierta la puerta a un nuevo aplazamiento... aunque las probabilidades juegan claramente a su favor. El precedente de la pasada temporada también invita al optimismo. Antonelli firmó entonces una sólida sexta posición en México, un resultado que esta vez le permitiría proclamarse campeón del mundo. Tonybet paga a 1.06 que el italiano termine en zona de puntos, mientras que su victoria cotiza a 2.74, por los 2.36 de Max Verstappen. El joven piloto, sin embargo, no quiere conformarse con asegurar la corona: aspira a firmar una nueva pole y rematar el fin de semana por todo lo alto. Las apuestas deportivas apuntan a una batalla exigente, pero Antonelli tiene el campeonato al alcance de la mano. En cuanto a los españoles, el objetivo pasa por dejar atrás otro fin de semana decepcionante, esta vez en Singapur. Carlos Sainz terminó decimocuarto con su Williams, mientras que Fernando Alonso cruzó la meta en decimosexta posición con el Aston Martin. Ambos necesitan dar un paso adelante en México para volver a pelear por los puntos. Tonybet paga a 11.0 que Sainz termine entre los diez primeros y a 6.5 que lo consiga Alonso. Las mejores casas de apuestas también siguen pendientes de la lucha por el Mundial, pero todas las miradas estarán puestas en Antonelli: si cumple con su cometido, la Fórmula 1 tendrá nuevo campeón a falta de dos citas para el final. articles.title: Monchi aprieta el botón del pánico
articles.standfirst: El Espanyol prescindió de los servicios de Manolo González tras la eliminación en Copa del Rey contra el Sestao
articles.summary: El Espanyol prescindió de los servicios de Manolo González tras la eliminación en Copa del Rey contra el Sestao
articles.body: La situación del Espanyol lleva meses siendo preocupante. La pasada temporada, el conjunto perico pasó de soñar con meterse en Europa a pelear hasta el final por evitar el descenso. Pese a ello, la directiva decidió mantener su confianza en Manolo González, el técnico que había devuelto al equipo a Primera en 2024. Sin embargo, los resultados no han acompañado y la situación parece haberse enquistado hasta el punto de que Monchi ha decidido apretar el botón del pánico para tratar de enderezar el rumbo de una temporada que empieza a complicarse demasiado pronto. La decisión de prescindir del entrenador llegó después de la eliminación en la Copa del Rey frente al Sestao, conjunto de Segunda Federación. Un golpe difícil de digerir para una afición que esperaba que el torneo copero sirviera para recuperar sensaciones y cambiar la dinámica. La derrota terminó por precipitar una decisión que llevaba tiempo barruntándose en los despachos, con un equipo que no encontraba la manera de levantar el vuelo. Los números en Liga explican buena parte de la decisión. El Espanyol acumula cinco jornadas consecutivas sin ganar y apenas ha sumado un punto de los últimos 15 posibles. Una racha que le ha llevado a cerrar la jornada 10 en puestos de descenso y que ha terminado por agotar el crédito de Manolo González. El margen de reacción empieza a reducirse y el club necesita encontrar cuanto antes una solución que permita recuperar la confianza y alejarse de una zona baja que vuelve a amenazar con convertirse en una pesadilla. Pese a este escenario, 777 todavía no sitúa al Espanyol entre los tres principales candidatos a perder la categoría. Su descenso cotiza a 4.50, por encima de equipos como el Málaga, con una cuota de 1.50; el Racing, a 2.38; el Getafe, a 3.50; y el Valencia y el Levante, ambos a 4.0. No obstante, hay un precedente que invita a la cautela: el Espanyol ha firmado su peor arranque liguero desde la temporada 2019-20, cuando también acumulaba ocho puntos después de 10 jornadas y acabó perdiendo la categoría. Las apuestas deportivas reflejan que todavía hay margen para reaccionar, pero el equipo necesita transformar esa posibilidad en resultados. A la espera de que Monchi anuncie quién será el sustituto de Manolo González, el objetivo pasa por cortar la mala dinámica cuanto antes. No será una tarea sencilla, ya que el próximo compromiso llevará al Espanyol hasta La Cerámica para medirse al Villarreal. Los pericos necesitarán dar un paso al frente ante un rival exigente si quieren empezar a salir del pozo. 777 paga a 6.40 la victoria blanquiazul. Una cuota que refleja la dificultad del desafío. Las mejores casas de apuestas seguirán pendientes de la reacción del equipo, que necesita un cambio de rumbo urgente para evitar que la temporada vuelva a convertirse en una lucha agónica por la permanencia.

articles.summary: Para Tonybet es el favorito a alzarse con el título en Viena, por primera vez
articles.body: El Erste Bank Open, ATP 500 que se disputa en pista dura cubierta del Wiener Stadthalle entre el 26 de octubre y el 1 de noviembre, reúne esta semana a seis jugadores del top 10. Es un torneo que sirve de ensayo para el tramo final de la temporada, con el Masters 1000 de París y las ATP Finals en el horizonte, y varios tenistas se juegan algo más que el trofeo. Un cambio de última hora en el calendario, provocado por el aplazamiento del Six Kings Slam, ha traído a la capital austriaca a uno de los grandes nombres del circuito. Las casas de apuestas ya tienen claro quién manda en el mercado. Para Tonybet, Carlos Alcaraz es el favorito, con una cuota de 1.95 que lo sitúa casi como un candidato a ganar de cada dos opciones. Llega a Viena por primera vez desde 2021, cuando cayó ante Zverev, y nunca ha levantado este título. Con un balance de 33 victorias y cinco derrotas en la temporada, busca su cuarto título del año y el número 28 de su carrera. La cuota refleja su jerarquía, aunque también algo de confianza ajena. El murciano aún busca su mejor versión en pista cubierta y tiene un cuadro nada sencillo. Debutó ante Karen Khachanov y su camino pasa por posibles duelos con Tommy Paul en cuartos y con Medvedev o Mensik en semifinales. A no mucha distancia en las apuestas deportivas, aparece Alexander Zverev, a cuota 3.99. El alemán es cabeza de serie número uno, excampeón de Viena y llega con la opción de alcanzar por primera vez en su carrera el número uno del mundo si los resultados le acompañan. Conoce bien esta pista y, tras un debut duro ante Martín Landaluce, afronta un cuadro con Cobolli, De Miñaur y Tiafoe en su mitad. Al estar en el lado contrario, solo podría cruzarse con Alcaraz en la final, un enfrentamiento que el mercado da casi por hecho. Alex de Miñaur cotiza a 9.96. El australiano es quinto cabeza de serie y ocupa el puesto ocho del ranking, con un tenis sólido y muy regular, especialmente efectivo en pistas rápidas. Su camino pasa por la zona de Zverev, un obstáculo importante que el mercado ya tiene en cuenta. Es un jugador que rara vez da un mal partido, aunque le suele faltar el punto extra para ganar grandes finales ante los mejores. Daniil Medvedev comparte esa misma cuota, 9.96. El ruso es tercer cabeza de serie, ocupa el quinto puesto mundial y se encuentra en plena lucha por un billete a las ATP Finals, lo que le obliga a sumar puntos. Su juego plano y su fortaleza en pista dura cubierta le convierten en un rival incómodo para cualquiera, y su posible duelo con Alcaraz en semifinales sería uno de los grandes alicientes del torneo. A su favor juega el hecho de que su cuota recoge a un jugador con experiencia en las rondas finales, pero también la irregularidad que ha mostrado esta temporada. Cierra la lista de aspirantes Tommy Paul, a 14.9. El estadounidense, séptimo cabeza de serie, aparece en la misma zona del cuadro que Alcaraz, con quien podría verse las caras en cuartos de final. Es un jugador capaz de poner en apuros a cualquiera cuando su saque funciona, pero su cuota refleja que el mercado lo ve como un rival para frenar al favorito, más que como un candidato real al título. articles.title: What Makes These Brewers Special? Jeter, Papi, A-Rod Laud World Series Champs
articles.summary: FOX Sports' Derek Jeter, David Ortiz, and Alex Rodriguez reflect on what made the Milwaukee Brewers the ultimate World Series champions.
articles.body: Forty-four years in the making, the Milwaukee Brewers are the 2026 World Series champions. With a deep roster and dominance on both sides of the ball, the Brewers earned the franchise's first ever title. For the MLB on FOX crew, Milwaukee proved why the Brewers were the team to beat for multiple reasons. "This has cemented them now as one of the best overall teams that we've seen in a long time," FOX Sports' Derek Jeter said. "And in this day and age, when everyone's trying to hit home runs, they don't worry about strikeouts. You have a team like the Milwaukee Brewers that play situational baseball." Following a campaign in which they led MLB with 103 wins and won the NL Central for the fourth straight season, the Brewers dominated October. Their postseason record (11-2) included beating the Padres in the NLDS and then sweeping the Dodgers in the NLCS. The Brewers were so dominant they allowed fewer than five runs and 10 hits – while striking out at least five batters – in each of their final 18 games across both the regular season and postseason. FOX Sports' David "Big Papi" Ortiz emphasized what made Milwaukee dominant: their success at the plate and their ability to stay on offense made for a memorable World Series. "They play the game right. They move the runner over. They get on base. They run the bases perfectly fine. They play good defense. They got great pitching. They have an old-school manager [in Pat Murphy] who basically keeps them put all year round, and that's why they dominate the National League," Ortiz said. On a team that doesn't have a standout star, it was their collection of talented players that shined at this World Series. Brewers' ace Jacob Misiorowski, who'll likely win the NL Cy Young award, pitched an unstoppable 5.2 innings in Game 5 before coming off with an apparent cramp. World Series MVP William Contreras dominated on the diamond, hitting .381 and going 8-for-21 during the series. He showed his talent behind the plate, throwing out four runners trying to steal base and winning 10 Automated Ball-Strike challenges. For FOX Sports' Alex Rodriguez, beyond playing good baseball by the book, the elements that made Milwaukee the final team standing created the perfect love story for the Brewers' first-ever title. "This is an impossible love story; an impossible team not to admire," Rodriguez said. "From top to bottom, the character, the A-plus roster construction, young guys, 9 to 10 guys under the age of 28, but they play like veterans."

articles.title: Los Brewers se estrenan como campeones de las Series Mundiales
articles.standfirst: Milwaukee gana por primera vez la MLB después de vencer en el quinto encuentro a los Rays 1-4 y firmar un curso histórico: mejor equipo en la temporada regular y 11-2 en los playoffs
articles.summary: Milwaukee gana por primera vez la MLB después de vencer en el quinto encuentro a los Rays 1-4 y firmar un curso histórico: mejor equipo en la temporada regular y 11-2 en los playoffs
articles.body: Milwaukee Bravos ganó las Series Mundiales en 1957 de la mano de Hank Aaron, leyenda del béisbol. Pero aquel campeonato no sirvió de mucho en la ciudad de Wisconsin. Los Bravos finalmente se mudaron a Atlanta, donde siguen. Desde entonces, 58 años, Milwaukee no había tenido un campeón en el deporte más americano para los estadounidenses. Hasta hace unas horas, culminando una temporada histórica, los Brewers, fundados en 1969, consiguieron el triunfo en el Tropicana Field de St. Petersburg (Florida) tras vencer 1-4 a los Rays para alcanzar el primer título de su historia en la edición 123ª de las Series Mundiales. El venezolano William Contreras, campeón del Clásico Mundial con su país, fue elegido MVP. "Es el mejor equipo de la MLB contra el que he jugado y llevo siete temporadas en la Liga", dijo Drew Rasmussen, abridor de los Rays. La impresión no es exagerada, incluso pensando en el dominio de los Dodgers en 2024 y 2025. Los Brewers fueron el mejor equipo en temporada regular con 103 y cuando el mundo del béisbol profesional pensaba que no podían mejorar, Milwaukee ha firmado unos playoffs aplastantes con un balance de 11-2. Desde septiembre, cuando la temporada se pone 'seria', el equipo dirigido por Pat Murphy ha ganado 26 de 31 partidos. “Pienso en la ciudad de Milwaukee, en el estado de Wisconsin. Sin duda, nos impulsaron a seguir adelante, y este grupo de muchachos, este equipo de 2026, será recordado para siempre. Se lo merecen, porque eran un verdadero equipo, y no podría estar más agradecido ni más orgulloso de ser parte de esto”, dijo el entrenador de 67 años (el más mayor del campeonato), que ha construido una máquina perfecta: los Brewers fueron el segundo en la temporada en número de carreras, quintos en bases robadas y primero en porcentaje de bases por bolas. Lideraron en promedio de bateo. En defensa, fueron segundos en efectividad colectiva. Los Brewers ganaron un título muy merecido después de fracasar hace 44 años en su primer y único intento en las Series Mundiales (cayeron 4-0 ante los Cardinals). Y dejaron de pertenecer al club de las franquicias que nunca han sido campeones. Allí siguen los Rays junto a Seattle Mariners, Colorado Rockies y San Diego Padres. Contreras fue elegido MVP. "No sé cómo lo hago, pero siempre estoy ahí", dijo el venezolano, que hace siete meses había ganado con su selección el Clásico Mundial tras derrotar a Estados Unidos. Los Brewers se ha convertido en el tercer equipo de la historia en conseguir el título y ganar 100 partidos y el primero en hacerlo desde los Mets en 1969. Wisconsin, frío y olvidado, es el tercer estado del país desde 2010 en ser campeón de la NBA (Bucks), NFL (Packers) y MLB (Brewers). Los otros dos son Massachusetts y California.

articles.title: Roll The Tape: Goff Is Built To Beat Minnesota; Why McCarthy Is Thriving In New York
articles.summary: After diving into the All-22 coaches' film from Week 7, Bucky Brooks examines three new developments to watch.
articles.body: The Seahawks reminded why they have the best defense in football. The Lions have an ideal quarterback to spoil the Vikings' perfect record. The Giants might have a new starting quarterback. Each week, I dive into the All-22 coaches' film before offering a few insights to watch. Here are three developments that could be long-term storylines involving some of the best teams and players in the NFL. 1.How Seattle Shut Down Old Friend Kenneth Walker III Whenever a defense gets to face a former teammate who has teased and tormented them in practices for years, the unit can’t wait to spot the ball and shut down their ex to earn bragging rights. With star running back Kenneth Walker III returning to Seattle to face the league’s top defense in prime time this past week, the football world couldn’t wait to see how the "Dark Side" would treat K9 in his homecoming. Walker, of course, didn't enter the matchup as merely the reigning Super Bowl MVP. He was the NFL’s rushing leader after averaging a whopping 133 yards per game while forcing 51 missed tackles through five games. The fifth-year pro was picking up 9.2 yards per carry when not hit behind the line of scrimmage, which led the NFL by over a full yard (minimum 25 carries). However, the Seahawks are a sure-tackling team, with a 90.1% tackling rate (third-highest) and hit running backs in the backfield on 48.5% of their carries, with 22.7% of those hits resulting in a tackle for loss or no gain. A long, hard look at the tape from this Week 7 showdown revealed a lot about the Seahawks. Namely, they boast the best defense in football. Defensive-minded head coach Mike Macdonald has installed a scheme that lets his playmakers play fast, but from various spots and alignments. As a proponent of positionless football, the Seahawks run five and six defensive backs on the field at all times, and their clever use of Nickel and Dime personnel, regardless of the offensive grouping, speaks to the unit's versatility, with defensive backs deployed as quasi-linebackers on blitzes. Against Kansas City, Seattle didn’t stray from that approach, playing five or more defensive backs on 100% of the snaps. With Macdonald keeping his defensive backs deep to eliminate explosives through the air, the Seahawks impressively kept Walker in check without loading the box. They finished with a 7.1% stacked-box rate, per Next Gen Stats, while holding the Chiefs to 4.3 yards per play and limiting Walker to just 36 rushing yards total. The stellar performance snapped Walker’s 11-game streak with at least 50 yards and offered a blueprint for containing the NFL’s top rusher. Studying the All-22 coaches’ footage, the Seahawks contained the Super Bowl MVP with a high school-like game plan featured on Friday nights across the country. The defense stayed in a traditional two-deep zone or single-high safety coverage with five defensive backs on the field. They overwhelmed the Chiefs at the point of attack with interior size and outran Walker to the corner, with a speedy collection of linebackers and defensive backs running the ball with urgency. Seattle's outstanding effort and flawless tackling stopped Walker in his tracks and disrupted the rhythm of an offense that has dictated its terms to opponents with a balanced but explosive attack. Although Macdonald added some tricks and gimmicks throughout the game, the Seahawks simply overwhelmed the Chiefs with their talent, toughness and tenacity. If they continue to play to their standard, the defending champs will have a lot to say about which team represents the NFC in Super Bowl LXI. 2.Will Vikings Alter Approach Against Lions' Blitz-Beating QB? Under aggressive defensive coordinator Brian Flores, the Minnesota Vikings have lived and died by the blitz. But the blitz-heavy tactician’s diabolical methods will be tested Sunday against Jared Goff and the Detroit Lions in America's Game of the Week (1 p.m. ET on FOX). The Vikings enter Week 8 with the highest blitz rate in the NFL, coming off a game in which they registered the highest blitz rate in a single game (85.2%) in the Next Gen Stats era. Flores has pummeled quarterbacks into submission with an exotic pressure scheme that taxes the mind, body and soul. His unit relentlessly stresses opponents with five- and six-man pressures, complemented by simulated blitzes that radically change the picture for quarterbacks, with only four defenders rushing and seven falling back into coverage. Flores' psychotic, high-pressure approach has turned the Vikings into a defensive juggernaut, and the football world is buzzing. In studying the All-22 coaches’ footage from the Vikings’ 16-10 win in Week 7 over the Colts, persistent pressure and constant harassment forced Daniel Jones into one of the worst performances of his career (he completed 13 of 22 passes for 108 yards and an interception), as Minnesota scratched out its sixth win with minimal contributions from the offense. Although Jones wilted under pressure, the Vikings will face an unflappable quarterback this weekend in Goff. The former No. 1 overall pick has become comfortable amid chaos, as shown by his remarkable numbers against the blitz. He enters Week 8 with a higher completion percentage (70% to 66%), passer rating (123.3 to 107.5) and yards per attempt (8.2 to 7.9) when blitzed compared to coverage. He surgically carves up defenses when under pressure, whether blitzes come up the middle or off the edges to disrupt his rhythm. Goff’s poise and pinpoint accuracy let him punish opponents for risky approaches. Against the Vikings, Goff must be prepared for "all-out" blitzes with everyone attacking the pocket from "mug" alignments (both linebackers positioned in the gap between the center and guard). An ultra-aggressive blitz from a hyper-aggressive alignment sets the tone for the rest of the game because it immediately speeds up the clock for the QB, forcing him to face his fear of a physical beatdown. Additionally, constant pre-snap movement and post-snap trickery can lead to countless mistakes and blunders from newbies and veterans alike. Moreover, it creates a scary-movie effect, making Flores the "Boogeyman" everyone fears around this time of year. Given his experience against Flores and his high-pressure scheme, Goff has a chance to crack the code on a defensive scheme that has quarterbacks and playcallers up late at night. 3.J.J. McCarthy, Giants' QB Of The Future? Before you laugh at the thought of Minnesota castoff J.J. McCarthy becoming a permanent QB1 for his new squad, consider how the former first-rounder has quickly adapted to the Giants’ culture and energized an offense that suddenly looks competent under his direction. Perhaps we shouldn’t be surprised by his early success after connecting with John Harbaugh, who likely received operating instructions from his brother on how to maximize the young quarterback’s talent. It was just a few years ago, after all, that McCarthy led Jim Harbaugh's Michigan Wolverines to a 28-1 record and a national championship while running an old-school offense that bludgeoned opponents with a hard-hitting running game and a complementary aerial attack. Although skeptics questioned whether McCarthy could carry an offense as a designated playmaker, Jim Harbaugh advocated for him, calling McCarthy the "best quarterback" in the 2024 class during league meetings and after Michigan’s Pro Day. Harbaugh praised McCarthy's arm talent, intangibles and competitiveness, and highlighted his exceptional command of the Wolverines’ offense. In New York, McCarthy has been as good as advertised despite his struggles with the Vikings. The underrated dual-threat has energized the Giants’ offense with his playmaking potential, adding an explosive element to an offense that needed a shot of energy. Despite playing less than a quarter of Week 6, McCarthy connected on five passes for at least 20 yards. That tied a career-high. After adding another five such completions in Week 7 — he trails only Caleb Williams (11) in the entire league over the past two weeks — it is time for the football world to reconsider its opinion of the polarizing passer. John Harbaugh’s tough love and blue-collar environment, combined with offensive coordinator Matt Nagy’s experience with young quarterbacks (see: Mitch Trubisky) leading playoff-caliber teams, could give the Giants a chance to hang onto the NFC East crown by season’s end. The Giants’ new QB1 has the right mix of gunslinger and game manager to enhance a ground-and-pound offense and complement an aggressive defense that can control the game with a dynamic crew of defensive linemen and linebackers. Should the Giants continue to build confidence with McCarthy under center, don't be surprised if he ultimately forces an unexpected QB competition in 2027 with Jaxson Dart that determines which former first-rounder owns the starting job for years to come.

articles.title: Defending champ shoots 63 at Te Arai, leads Asia-Pacific Amateur by 3 in New Zealand
articles.summary: Defending champion Fifa Laopakdee fired an 8-under 63 to take a three-shot lead at the Asia-Pacific Amateur.
articles.body:
Fifa Laopakdee made history last fall becoming the first player from Thailand to win the Asia-Pacific Amateur Championship in Dubai. Now he's trying to become the second player to win consecutive AAC titles, and he's off to a thrilling start.

Laopakdee, a senior at Arizona State, fired a stellar 8-under 63 on Thursday at Te Arai Links in New Zealand to take a three-shot lead after the opening round. He carded seven birdies and an eagle, a hole out from 83 yards on the par-4 ninth hole.

"Couldn't ask for a better way to start the round," Laopakdee said. "8 under wasn't on my bingo card today but able to pull it off. It feels pretty amazing."

Laopakdee leads New Zealand native Joshua Bai, whose 66 featured six birdies and only one blemish on the scorecard. Kiwis Cooper Moore and Ryan Xie are tied for third at 4 under.

Laopakdee's round was one stroke shy of the championship scoring record (62). Last year, he won on the third playoff hole to lock up spots in the Masters and Open Championship.

This year, he's trying to join Hideki Matsuyama as the only players to win consecutive Asia-Pacific Amateur titles and the third golfer to win the championship twice.

"Definitely one of the best rounds I've played this year by far," Laopakdee said. "As I said in the press conference, I didn't have my best golf this year, and it's nice to see that I'm still capable of playing how I played today in this kind of condition."

Laopakdee's round was stellar, coming in the afternoon in windy conditions. At Te Arai, where a majority of holes have views of the Pacific Ocean, the wind is often a factor, but Laopakdee was able to fight through the wind and dominate the opening day.

Heading into the second round, the projected cut is 5 over. The top-60 players and ties will advance to the weekend.

The winner earns exemptions into the 2027 Masters and Open Championship at St Andrews.

Cameron Jourdan is an assistant editor of Golfweek, covering college and amateur golf, the PGA Tour and plenty more. Follow Cameron on X/Twitter (@Cam_Jourdan) or Instagram (@GolfweekJourdan).

articles.title: In Photos: Rodtang Shows Off His Firepower Ahead Of World Grand Prix Showdown With Nong-O
articles.summary: The former flyweight king puts his skills on display before the long-awaited clash of Thai icons.
articles.body:
Former ONE Flyweight Muay Thai World Champion Rodtang "The Iron Man" Jitmuangnon gave the media a glimpse of his preparations during an open workout at Jitmuangnon Gym in Nonthaburi, Thailand, on Wednesday, October 28.

The 29-year-old Thai megastar displayed his trademark intensity as he sharpened his weapons ahead of his highly anticipated showdown with legendary former ONE Bantamweight Muay Thai World Champion Nong-O Hama .

The two icons will finally collide in the 2026-2027 ONE Flyweight Muay Thai World Grand Prix quarterfinals at The Inner Circle 38 on Friday, November 13, live in Asia primetime from Bangkok's Lumpinee Stadium, streaming exclusively for members at live.onefc.com .

Originally scheduled to meet at ONE 173 last November, Rodtang and Nong-O now have the opportunity to settle their unfinished business, with a place in the tournament semifinals and a step toward World Title glory at stake.

Rodtang: 'The Iron Man' Reloads For Another Shot At Gold

One of the most electrifying strikers in Muay Thai history, Rodtang has amassed 274 career victories and a 17-3 record in ONE Championship, captivating audiences with his relentless aggression, granite chin, and devastating punching combinations.

The #2-ranked flyweight Muay Thai contender previously ruled the division for five years, successfully defending his ONE World Title five times before being stripped of the crown in 2024.

Now, following his return to ONE Championship under a new contract earlier this year, the Jitmuangnon Gym representative is determined to reclaim his place at the summit.

His latest preparations have included intensive conditioning and training alongside fellow Thai standout Nuenglanlek Jitmuangnon , as he readies himself for a potentially career-defining battle with one of his childhood heroes.

Nong-O: A Childhood Idol Becomes A Formidable Rival

Standing in Rodtang's path is a man whose extraordinary career helped inspire an entire generation of Thai fighters.

At 39, Nong-O remains one of Muay Thai's most revered figures, with 268 professional victories and eight ONE Bantamweight Muay Thai World Title wins to his name.

The #3-ranked flyweight Muay Thai contender has since set his sights on becoming a two-division ONE World Champion, bringing his exceptional timing, technical mastery, and punishing right kicks into a new championship pursuit.

For Rodtang, the matchup carries special significance. He grew up admiring Nong-O's skills and considers the contest an opportunity to test himself against a master of the sport.

But once the opening bell rings, mutual respect will give way to fierce competition as two of Thailand's greatest modern strikers battle for a place in the Grand Prix semifinals.

articles.title: Maxx Crosby Has Strong Message Amid Raiders’ Four-Game Losing Streak
articles.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are riding a four-game losing streak after starting the season 3-0. Moreover, it might be a now-or-never situation heading into Week 8...
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders are riding a four-game losing streak after starting the season 3-0. Moreover, it might be a now-or-never situation heading into Week 8 against the New York Jets.

If the Silver and Black can get a win against New York, they get themselves back to .500. However, a loss against the Jets and the Raiders could see their losing streak go to six games, given that they'll face the San Francisco 49ers in their next contest.

Nonetheless, while there can be negativity around a losing streak, the Raiders' Maxx Crosby isn't allowing that to reach the team's dressing room, as he had a message for the doubters who don't believe Las Vegas can turn their situation around.

"You play to win," Crosby told reporters on Oct. 28. "We're playing to try to make the playoffs and win. That's what we do. I try not to pay attention to it. I feel like it's probably the least amount of attention I pay to all the outside noise. But negativity is just how our world operates these days, and that's what sells.

"If you want to be negative and not believe, then stay over there. Stay on that side because I know when things turn around or when you win, all those tough people just disappear, and then they come back when it's convenient. But that's just what life is like. That's how the world is, unfortunately."

Maxx Crosby: Team Is Using Doubters as Motivation

Moreover, Crosby relayed the message regarding the team being doubted that they can turn this situation around, which they are trying to use as fuel to motivate the team heading into Week 8.

"I know these guys in the locker room want to win so bad, but it doesn't mean you can't be optimistic," Crosby added. "You have to be optimistic [and] you have to love this game and put everything into it, even when everybody is against you and everyone thinks it's the same old story. You have to go win, and that's how you shut everybody up.

"So I love being doubted. I've been doubted my whole life, so keep it coming. I appreciate that. You just make it a bigger monster. I know this locker room is the same way. We're all extremely motivated, and I know guys are ready to go out there and shut everybody up."

Raiders, Cowboys Get Blockbuster Trade Idea

Meanwhile, the losing streak has allowed for the Crosby trade speculation to resurface. Recently, in an Oct. 27 video from 105.3 The FAN , former NFL offensive lineman Mark Schlereth was asked whether he would do a trade that involved Crosby and the Cowboys sending wideout George Pickens the other way, along with other parts, as part of a blockbuster trade.

"Oh yeah, would I do that? I'd do that in a heartbeat," Schlereth said. "I wouldn't even think twice about it. George Pickens will wow you with the spectacular. That dude will make some spectacular plays. He had the touchdown catch, which was phenomenal, right?

"He'll make those, but there'll be plenty of times during the course of the game when you'll put on the film and he's just standing around killing grass. So, yeah, would I do that? I would do that without even thinking twice about it."

articles.title: Why did the New Jersey Devils make a puzzling Connor Hellebuyck move just days after a blockbuster NHL trade
articles.summary: The New Jersey Devils made headlines by sidelining Connor Hellebuyck just days after acquiring him in a major trade, leaving fans wondering about the team's goaltending strategy and Hellebuyck's role moving forward.
articles.body: The New Jersey Devils raised questions about their goaltending plans after Connor Hellebuyck was left out of the lineup entirely for their game against the Colorado Avalanche. The decision came just one game after the star goalie made his first start for New Jersey following a major trade from Winnipeg.Jake Allen was named the starter, with Rémi Poirier serving as backup. The Devils did not publicly explain why Hellebuyck was given the night off, leaving his status a subject of speculation.Why New Jersey Devils rested Connor Hellebuyck after NHL debutThe New Jersey Devils gave Connor Hellebuyck a complete night off against the Colorado Avalanche, choosing Jake Allen to start and Rémi Poirier as the backup. The decision stood out because Hellebuyck had only just returned to game action in his first start for New Jersey.Devils reporter Amanda Stein reported before puck drop that Allen would start in goal, with Poirier backing him up. Hellebuyck was not listed as either the starter or backup, an unusual sight so soon after his arrival through a blockbuster trade.The decision prompted questions among fans, with some speculating about a possible injury. However, the available report did not confirm that Hellebuyck was hurt, and the Devils had not publicly offered a specific explanation for his absence. It would therefore be premature to describe the situation as an injury concern.Allen’s selection gave New Jersey an experienced option against Colorado. The veteran goaltender has a history of handling NHL starts, while Poirier provided the team’s backup option for the matchup.The decision also highlighted the importance of goaltending depth during a demanding regular-season schedule. Even after making a major move to acquire an established star, the Devils still need other goaltenders who can step in when required.What does the decision mean for Connor Hellebuyck’s future?Hellebuyck’s absence raises questions, but it does not establish that the Devils have concerns about his long-term role. A full rest could reflect workload management, particularly after a lengthy period away from game action, although the team has not confirmed that explanation.The timing made the move particularly noticeable: Hellebuyck had only just made his first start for New Jersey after the trade saga that kept him away from regular game action in Winnipeg. Yet one lineup decision is not enough to conclude that the team’s plans have changed.The next meaningful indicator will be the Devils’ updates on Hellebuyck’s availability and his place in the upcoming rotation. Until New Jersey provides further details, the reason for his absence remains uncertain.For now, Allen’s start against Colorado gave the Devils an opportunity to rely on their goaltending depth while Hellebuyck rested away from the lineup. The move was unexpected given the timing of his return, but any conclusions about an injury or a deeper issue would go beyond the confirmed information.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 7 NFL teams with best chance to win Super Bowl LXI entering Week 8
articles.summary: Week 7 finally knocked some shine off the NFL‘s heavyweights. San Francisco lost its perfect record in a four-turnover mess. Kansas City managed three points...
articles.body:
Week 7 finally knocked some shine off the NFL 's heavyweights. San Francisco lost its perfect record in a four-turnover mess. Kansas City managed three points against Seattle. Cincinnati buried Baltimore with 35 unanswered points. Minnesota remained unbeaten while somehow making a 16-10 victory feel like another warning about its offense. The championship picture didn't get turned upside down, but a few cracks became considerably harder to ignore.

That's the difference between ranking good teams and identifying legitimate Super Bowl contenders. Quarterback play, protection, defensive resilience, and the ability to win multiple ways matter more than collecting impressive Sundays. A great record can hide a serious weakness. One ugly loss can expose a problem without erasing six weeks of evidence.

Minnesota beat Indianapolis 16-10, and Brian Flores' defense practically dragged the offense across the finish line. The Vikings held the Colts to 64 net passing yards while blitzing on an extraordinary 85.2 percent of dropbacks.

Kyler Murray delivered the decisive late scramble, but threw for just 150 yards against a two-win opponent. The defense leads the league in EPA allowed per play, while the offense ranks 29th. Aaron Jones' aggravated MCL injury and declining blocking depth only complicate an attack already dependent on isolated moments of quarterback improvisation.

Detroit is next, giving Flores a fascinating matchup against one of the league's most efficient offenses. Buffalo and San Francisco loom in November, providing even better tests of Minnesota's offensive limitations. There's plenty to respect about a 6-0 team with a defense capable of suffocating almost anybody.

But championships generally demand more than asking that defense to perform a rescue operation every Sunday. Until Murray and the offense produce something more sustainable, Minnesota's undefeated record isn't enough to move it higher.

Cincinnati's 35-13 demolition of Baltimore was a reminder of how quickly Joe Burrow can hijack a football game. Trailing 13-0, the Bengals scored touchdowns on five consecutive possessions, with Burrow completing 16 of 18 passes for 249 yards and four touchdowns after halftime.

Tee Higgins contributed 148 receiving yards, and improved tackle protection is helping Burrow exploit a receiving corps that already terrifies defenses. The concern is an inefficient rushing attack and a defense that remains vulnerable to quarterback mobility and perimeter breakdowns. Beating Tyler Huntley doesn't answer every question about stopping elite opponents.

Tennessee visits Sunday, giving Cincinnati an opportunity to establish control without another spectacular comeback. Atlanta follows in Madrid, while Pittsburgh, Kansas City and a Baltimore rematch will provide more meaningful championship tests.

Cincinnati climbs because Burrow's passing game offers a reliable January scoring formula, especially with Chase and Higgins healthy. The Bengals don't have the defensive consistency or complementary rushing identity of the teams above them, but they're becoming considerably more dangerous as their protection improves.

Previous: Unranked | Back in the top seven

Seattle didn't merely beat Kansas City. It embarrassed an offense that rarely experiences anything resembling a helpless Sunday. The Seahawks held Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs to 213 yards, 11 first downs and zero red-zone possessions in a 20-3 victory.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba delivered 150 receiving yards, Emanuel Wilson rushed for 100 and Mike Macdonald's defense looked capable of dismantling anybody. The concern is whether the offense can repeat its contribution. Seattle still ranks 24th in offensive EPA per play, and Sam Darnold's end-zone interception was another reminder that turnovers and inconsistent protection haven't disappeared.

Acquiring All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson, pending his physical, could address a major weakness. He's allowed no sacks in 275 pass-blocking snaps this season, although he obviously had nothing to do with Sunday's victory. Chicago visits Monday, followed later by a San Francisco rematch and two remaining games against the Rams.

Those matchups will reveal whether Seattle's offense can become dependable enough to complement an elite defense. The Chiefs victory earns the Seahawks a return to the top seven. Sustaining that offensive improvement is what could make this team genuinely frightening in January.

Jacksonville rested in Week 7, leaving its 34-31 loss to Houston in London as the latest evidence. Trevor Lawrence threw for 306 yards and four touchdowns, but a costly end-zone interception and 426 yards allowed exposed problems that an explosive offense couldn't overcome.

Losing left tackle Anton Harrison to a season-ending ACL injury makes protection a substantial concern, particularly with Walker Little taking over. The defense remains excellent against the run, but its coverage hasn't been nearly as convincing. Jacksonville has enough offensive talent to threaten anybody; protecting Lawrence and preventing explosive passes are now the questions.

Indianapolis is up first before a Thursday trip to Baltimore, where the reshuffled offensive line gets to work. Chicago and a looming Houston rematch await later. Jacksonville is fourth in offensive EPA per play and seventh defensively, which reflects real chops more so than just one outstanding afternoon.

Liam Coen has built a versatile attack, and the defense provides enough resistance to survive an imperfect offense. That balance real, even if the occasional defensive lapses keep their championship case from feeling locked.

Buffalo enjoyed a Week 7 bye after beating Las Vegas 33-30, a game that perfectly captured the Bills' championship argument and its biggest problem. Josh Allen threw for 255 yards and two touchdowns without an interception, while James Cook contributed 153 yards from scrimmage. Buffalo scored on seven of nine meaningful possessions and continues to lead the league in offensive EPA per play.

Unfortunately, the defense ranks dead last in EPA allowed. The Raiders nearly erased a comfortable deficit, reinforcing the concern that Allen might spend January trying to rescue a defense incapable of protecting his work.

Baltimore visits Sunday with Lamar Jackson potentially returning, an immediate examination of Buffalo's defensive discipline. Minnesota's aggressive pressure awaits the following week, with Kansas City on Thanksgiving and Denver on Christmas providing additional playoff-caliber challenges.

Allen and Cook give Buffalo an extraordinary offensive ceiling, capable of winning through explosive passes, sustained drives, or a productive rushing attack. That's a championship foundation. But the Bills remain third because they haven't demonstrated the defensive reliability necessary to make that offense anything other than their primary survival mechanism.

There's no respectable way to dress up Kansas City's 20-3 loss in Seattle. The Chiefs generated 213 yards, 11 first downs and failed to reach the red zone for the first time in Patrick Mahomes' 153 career starts, including the playoffs. Kenneth Walker managed 36 rushing yards, and the offense never found an alternative.

Rashee Rice's absence, Jaylon Moore's concussion and Josh Simmons' continued absence exposed how vulnerable the passing game becomes when receiver depth and protection deteriorate simultaneously. For a team accustomed to solving problems, Kansas City spent Sunday looking completely out of answers.

Denver is next, with Nik Bonitto presenting an immediate test of the same protection issues Seattle exploited. Buffalo, the Rams, Cincinnati and San Francisco remain on the schedule. Kansas City stays second because Mahomes, Andy Reid and Steve Spagnuolo still provide one of football's strongest championship combinations.

The Chiefs rank fifth in both offensive and defensive EPA per play, and their defense remains capable of controlling games without demanding heroics from Mahomes. Seattle exposed a serious weakness, but one disastrous afternoon doesn't erase a season of excellent two-way football. It does eliminate much of Kansas City's margin for error.

San Francisco finally lost, falling 29-20 in Atlanta despite outgaining the Falcons 400-295. Four turnovers were the difference, including two Brock Purdy interceptions that undermined an otherwise productive offense. The 49ers remain second in offensive EPA per play and top 10 defensively, but the injury situation is becoming increasingly uncomfortable.

Christian McCaffrey is dealing with a mild hamstring strain, Nick Bosa has knee and calf issues, and the receiving corps remains depleted. Acquiring DeForest Buckner should strengthen a battered defensive front, but roster reinforcements don't automatically solve the turnover problem or restore everyone's health.

The Week 8 bye arrives at an excellent time, with Las Vegas waiting November 8 before more demanding matchups against Minnesota, Seattle, the Rams and Kansas City. Those games will test whether Kyle Shanahan can preserve the offense's explosive versatility while injuries continue reshaping his personnel.

San Francisco remains No. 1 because Purdy's efficiency, strong protection, Shanahan's adaptability and a credible defense still represent the most complete championship combination in football. The Atlanta loss exposed real vulnerabilities, and the 49ers are no longer comfortably separated from the field. But through seven games, nobody has assembled a stronger overall case to win Super Bowl LXI.

A 13-0 halftime lead against Cincinnati became a 35-13 loss, with five consecutive Bengals touchdown drives exposing the defense. Lamar Jackson is expected back, but his ankle remains untested in live action. Interior-line injuries and coverage breakdowns make Baltimore difficult to trust until its quarterback returns and the defense shows some resilience.

Matthew Stafford threw three touchdowns while Kyren Williams and Blake Corum combined for 192 rushing yards against Las Vegas. That's the offensive versatility Sean McVay needs. Unfortunately, Davante Adams' ruptured hamstring, Poona Ford's season-ending injury and uncertainty elsewhere on defense make this roster increasingly difficult to trust over a playoff run.

Caleb Williams and Ben Johnson are building something legitimate, and Chicago showed composure beating New England 30-24. Montez Sweat's return strengthens the defensive front. But protection, coverage discipline, and inconsistent efficiency remain concerns. Monday night's trip to Seattle offers a terrific opportunity to prove this team belongs with the established contenders.

Nik Bonitto generated 13 pressures against Arizona, and Denver's defense can absolutely dictate games. Bo Nix completed just 15 of 29 passes despite the 30-16 victory, again exposing an inconsistent passing attack. The Broncos have championship-caliber defensive traits. Their offense hasn't earned the same confidence, and Kansas City visits Sunday.

articles.title: After broken jaw nightmare against Anthony Joshua, Jake Paul sets December 24 return in Dubai
articles.summary: Jake Paul has set his return for Thursday, December 24, in Dubai.
articles.body: Jake Paul has set his return for Thursday, December 24, in Dubai. Anthony Joshua, the 37-year-old two-time unified heavyweight champion from Britain, broke the jaw of the YouTuber-turned-boxer in four places last December, and two surgeries followed. It will be the first fight since that night. Paul, 29, has been cleared medically to compete again. No broadcaster is confirmed for the card. Most Valuable Promotions co-founder Nakisa Bidarian says one name is in talks and another is firmly out. Paul has promised a knockout, though no opponent has signed to take one.When is Jake Paul fighting again after the broken jaw?Jake Paul will fight on Christmas Eve, a Thursday this year, in Dubai. Joshua ended their fight in round six with a right hand, and Paul has not boxed since.The 29-year-old says the setback changed nothing about what he is working toward. He has spent years taking risks against opponents few expected him to face, and he calls himself hungrier than ever. Dubai fits the plan because the city thinks big and does not believe in limits. Plenty of names are on the list, Paul says, and the contract is the only missing piece. His message to the city was a seasonal one: “Santa Paul is coming to town, and somebody’s getting knocked out.”Who will Jake Paul fight and why Christmas Eve?Ex-UFC fighter Darren Till, 33, is among those in talks, according to Bidarian, who co-founded MVP with Paul in 2021. Tommy Fury is not. Fury beat Paul in 2023, but Bidarian says his last offer came in Birmingham, at the promotion’s most recent event with Sky. The door only reopens if Fury shows up with a guarantee that suits Paul. Bidarian put it bluntly, “Tommy Fury, to be unequivocally clear, he got his last offer from us in Birmingham when we were there for our last MVPW event with Sky. And the only way Jake Paul’s ever going to face Tommy Fury is if Tommy Fury shows up with a guarantee that’s appropriate for Jake Paul,” Bidarian told SunSports. He added, “We are done giving that guy life-changing opportunities.”The holiday slot has been on MVP’s radar for a while. Bidarian says people are home with family and food, and most of what is on television is reruns or second-tier sports. Amazon has its first Christmas Eve NFL game this year, which backs up his point about a captive audience. Christmas Day is crowded in the US with the NBA and NFL going back to back, so he rates Christmas Eve as the better date. articles.title: YouTube star Jake Paul returns to boxing after Joshua loss for Dubai fight
articles.summary: American Jake Paul to headline Christmas Eve boxing event in Dubai, with his opponent yet to be announced.
articles.body:
YouTuber-turned-boxer Jake Paul will return to the ring on December 24 in Dubai just over a year after suffering a broken jaw in his knockout loss to Anthony Joshua, he said.

American Paul, 29, will headline the Christmas Eve card, with his opponent yet to be announced.

The bout will be Paul’s first since his sixth-round knockout loss to former heavyweight champion Joshua in Miami on December 19 last year, when his jaw was fractured in two places, injuries that required multiple surgeries in December and February.

“I have spent years proving people wrong, taking risks and pushing myself against opponents nobody thought I would face,” Paul said in a statement.

“Nothing that’s happened has changed my belief in myself or what I’m working toward. I am hungrier than ever and on December 24 I’m returning to the ring in Dubai to start the next chapter of my journey.

“We’ve got plenty of names on the list; let’s see who signs the contract,” he added.

Paul has a 12-2 professional record, with his only defeats coming against Britain’s Tommy Fury and Joshua.

He also fought Mike Tyson in an exhibition fight in which he beat the former heavyweight champion in a unanimous points decision, although the bout drew criticism as a sham event.

articles.title: Un chófer de Uber emprende la marcha y se lleva a un compañero sobre el capó
articles.standfirst: Los hechos han sucedido este miércoles poco antes de las 13h en la rotonda que da acceso al kilómetro 16 de la autovía A-1, a la altura de Alcobendas
articles.summary: Los hechos han sucedido este miércoles poco antes de las 13h en la rotonda que da acceso al kilómetro 16 de la autovía A-1, a la altura de Alcobendas
articles.body: Los pocos transeúntes que circulaban hoy poco antes de las 13h junto a la salida 16 de la A-1 se habrán sorprendido por una escena más de película que de vida real. Los hechos han sucedido en la enorme rotonda situada bajo la autovía, donde los gritos de un hombre extranjero (César, se llama) alertaban de que algo estaba sucediendo. No pedían auxilio, sino que exigían al conductor de otro Uber que no saliera de allí, que no abandonara la escena. Pero este ha arrancado llevándose consigo a su compañero de profesión sobre el capó. Todo ha sucedido cuando ambos iban a tomar la rotonda que da acceso a la A-1. En un momento dado, el conductor que va delante frena antes de entrar en la rotonda, que está concurrida a esas horas. El conductor que va detrás no frena a tiempo, de forma que golpea al coche de delante, hundiéndole la esquina del paragolpes. Tras la colisión, el conductor del coche golpeado sale y le pide a su compañero de trabajo que paren en el arcén para formalizar el parte del seguro. Pero el segundo conductor, que lleva a una mujer con dos menores de edad, se niega a ello. César se planta entonces delante del coche exigiéndole que baje del coche, cada vez en un tono más elevado. Hasta que el segundo Uber arranca y se lleva sobre el capó a César, que, asustado, no deja de gritar que detenga el coche mientras se agarra a los pilares del parabrisas para no caerse. El recorrido al final es corto, de no más de 25 metros. Y lo más sorprendente es que después de este momento, y todavía con los pasajeros, dentro no se enzarzan en una pelea cuando al final el segundo chófer para y se baja del coche. Una patrulla local de la policía de Alcobendas que pasaba a los pocos minutos se ha hecho cargo de la situación, conociendo lo sucedido gracias a este vídeo y llamando a una ambulancia para atender a César, al que una de las embestidas le ha dejado una pierna con lesiones.

articles.title: What Did Brewers Offer Tigers For Tarik Skubal, Who Ended Up With Dodgers?
articles.summary: A report detailed what the Brewers offered the Tigers for Tarik Skubal, who ended up on the Dodgers, at the MLB trade deadline.
articles.body: The Milwaukee Brewers dominated. After winning an MLB-best 103 games in the regular season, the Brewers defeated the San Diego Padres in four games in the National League Division Series, swept the Los Angeles Dodgers in the NL Championship Series and defeated the Tampa Bay Rays in five games in the 2026 World Series to capture their first championship. And the Brewers did it without acquiring defending, back-to-back Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal from the Detroit Tigers at the MLB trade deadline. Instead, Skubal landed in L.A. with the Dodgers and got handled by the Brewers in the NLCS. On that note, what was the Brewers' offer for Skubal? What Did Brewers Offer For Skubal? Milwaukee offered Detroit infield prospects Luis Peña (the Brewers' No. 2 prospect, per MLB Pipeline) and Jett Williams (Milwaukee's No. 10 prospect) and outfielder Josh Adamczewski (Milwaukee's 15th round pick in the 2023 MLB Draft) for Skubal, according to a report from The Athletic. However, Detroit sought more, preferably a top position player prospect and a starting pitcher under team control for the foreseeable future, most notably, Brewers right-hander Logan Henderson, which Milwaukee refused to do. Ultimately, the Tigers traded Skubal to the Dodgers for outfielder Zyhir Hope — who is now Detroit's top prospect, per MLB Pipeline — and right-handed pitchers River Ryan (the Dodgers' No. 7 prospect at the time of the trade) and Brady Smith (the Dodgers' No. 17 prospect when the deal was made). The Brewers pivoted, acquiring starting pitcher Dustin May and left-handed reliever JoJo Romero — who gave up just one run over eight innings this postseason — from the St. Louis Cardinals and right-handed reliever Antonio Senzatela from the Colorado Rockies. How Skubal Fared With Dodgers Skubal — whose 2026 campaign was sidetracked for six weeks due to an elbow injury and subsequent surgery — was terrific for the Dodgers, recording a 2.61 ERA, a 1.05 WHIP, a 162 ERA+ and 70 strikeouts across 62 innings pitched for the team in the regular season. Skubal then posted a 2.45 ERA, a 1.00 WHIP and 14 strikeouts over 11 innings across his two postseason starts for Los Angeles. Of course, Skubal's second postseason outing came against the Brewers, which was a 2-1 loss to open the NLCS for the Dodgers. Brewers Didn't Need Skubal Skubal, who will be 30 at the start of the 2027 MLB season, is set to hit free agency this offseason. Should the Brewers pursue Skubal on the open market, the superstar southpaw would add to a starting rotation that already includes likely 2026 NL Cy Young Award winner Jacob Misiorowski, the aforementioned Henderson and Robert Gasser, among others. In all, Milwaukee's starting rotation was second in MLB in opponent batting average (.220), third in strikeouts (907), tied for third in WHIP (1.14) and fifth outright in ERA (3.61) in the regular season. articles.title: Spanish long jumper Julieta Gallego among victims of deadly train collision
articles.summary: Julieta Gallego, who competed for Madrid-based AD Sprint, among those killed in train crash in Spain.
articles.body:
The Royal Spanish Athletics Federation expressed its condolences following the death of 24-year-old long jumper Julieta Gallego, who was among the victims of the train collision in Spain’s Toledo province that killed at least 68 people.

“The Spanish athletics family joins in the grief over the passing of Julieta Gallego, athlete of AD Sprint, in the train accident that occurred in Urda (Toledo),” the federation (RFEA) said in a statement on Thursday on X, offering its support to her family, friends and club teammates.

Gallego competed for Madrid-based AD Sprint and was a regular participant in Spain’s club championships. Her long jump personal best was 5.90 metres (19.4 feet), set in Antequera in 2023.

“There are blows that strike at the very heart of the athletics family. Today, the sport mourns the passing of Julieta, a life ahead of her that has been unjustly extinguished,” RFEA president Raul Chapado told Spanish newspaper ABC.

Two high-speed trains collided on Wednesday in the second deadly accident in less than a year on the line connecting Madrid to southern Andalusia.

At least 68 people were killed in the crash and about 80 were injured, 50 of them seriously and 15 critically, said Emiliano Garcia-Page, president of the Castilla-La Mancha regional government.

The most seriously injured people were taken to hospitals in the region and in Madrid, the capital. Others were assessed at a sports hall near the crash site, where emergency teams sorted them by the severity of their injuries before sending them home or to hospital.

Survivors treated near the scene had head wounds, facial swelling and bloodied clothing, and many were dazed, according to local media reports.

articles.title: New NHL Trade Rumors on Dylan Larkin After 'Escalated' Talks Around Red Wings Star
articles.summary: The monthslong standoff between the Detroit Red Wings and former captain Dylan Larkin could be nearing a conclusion.
articles.body:
The monthslong standoff between the Detroit Red Wings and former captain Dylan Larkin could be nearing a conclusion.

Red Wings coach Todd McLellan told reporters Thursday Larkin will not be playing Thursday night against the visiting Chicago Blackhawks, per Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman .

Friedman added the Red Wings will hold Larkin out until he is dealt to another team.

Which Teams Are Pretenders or Contenders? 🤔

Larkin's agent, Pat Brisson, said in a statement that the forward has "had enough of the situation."

Interim general manager Shawn Horcoff will address the situation later Thursday, McLellan added.

TSN's Pierre LeBrun reported the same day "trade talks have escalated on Larkin," who requested a trade this offseason and was subsequently stripped of his captaincy.

ESPN's Emily Kaplan added that "multiple teams" remain in the mix for Larkin and that the Minnesota Wild are believed to have made one of the "stronger offers" for the veteran.

Larkin, who holds a full no-trade clause, initially told the Red Wings he would only accept a trade to the Wild, Florida Panthers or Vegas Golden Knights, per Helene St. James of the Detroit Free Press .

As of last week that list had expanded to include the Dallas Stars, Washington Capitals, Carolina Hurricanes, Utah Mammoth, Tampa Bay Lightning, New Jersey Devils and Colorado Avalanche, St. James reported.

ESPN's Greg Wyshynski previously reported Larkin was not interested in playing for a Canadian team.

St. James previously reported Detroit is seeking a replacement for Larkin on the center of the top line with hopes of contending for a postseason spot in the near future.

Larkin, 30, is signed through the 2030-31 season with an $8.7 million AAV and full trade protections through the 2027-28 campaign.

Initial reporting regarding Larkin's offseason trade request preceded the organization parting ways with former GM Steve Yzerman.

The Red Wings have so far seen mixed results with Horcoff in his interim position. The franchise successfully finalized an extension with Alex DeBrincat, but let Patrick Kane walk in free agency and have yet to resolve an ongoing standoff with pending restricted free agent Simon Edvinsson.

Larkin started the regular season sidelined by what the Red Wings described as an upper body injury, but has since rejoined his team. He has since contributed six points (two goals, four assists) in 10 games for Detroit.

The Red Wings will hope ending the Larkin saga and getting back a potential first-line center, followed by the potential resolution of talks with Edvinsson, will help this team recover from a rocky 5-4-3 start and take a step toward ending the franchise's decade-long playoff drought.

articles.title: USC Coach Lincoln Riley Gives Vivid Response About Coaching Future
articles.summary: Amid speculation about his future in Los Angeles, USC head coach Lincoln Riley made his intentions crystal clear.
articles.body: Frustration is mounting, and a cloud of uncertainty hovers over Los Angeles. With that in mind, is USC Trojans head coach Lincoln Riley thinking about leaving? "If I didn't want to be at this place, I wouldn't have come here in the first place," Riley said when asked about his future at USC in a press conference Wednesday. "If I didn't want to be at this place, I've had plenty of opportunities to leave, and this is where I want to be. This is the right place for me. I'm the right person to be here. That's as honest and transparent as I can be with you." USC's 2026 Season Of Confusion While USC is 6-2, its wins have been a struggle and its losses have raised concerns. For starters, all the Trojans' Big Ten wins have come against teams with losing records in conference play, two of which have losing records on the season altogether in the Rutgers Scarlet Knights and Penn State Nittany Lions. Regarding the defeats, USC lost at home to Oregon in a game that saw Ducks starting quarterback Dante Moore get knocked out of the contest with a head injury. Then, last week, the Trojans — who were ranked No. 16 in the nation entering the week — were held to seven points in a loss on the road to the Wisconsin Badgers. USC is now unranked. USC's Mixed Results With Riley Following five seasons as the head coach at Oklahoma (2017-21), which saw the Sooners make the College Football Playoff in three consecutive years (2017-19) and win a double-digit number of games in four seasons, Riley left for USC following the 2021 regular season. In Riley's five seasons at USC, the Trojans are 41-20 and haven't made the College Football Playoff. In 2022, they had a chance to do so, but a loss to Utah in the Pac-12 Championship Game ended their playoff bid; USC left the Pac-12 for the Big Ten in the 2024 season. The 11 games the Trojans won in 2022 stand as the only time they've won a double-digit number of games under Riley. What's Lincoln Riley's Buyout Number? If USC decided to fire Riley, it would involve an estimated $70 million buyout. Riley originally signed a reported 10-year, $110 million contract with USC. Maryland, Baylor and NC State are the current Power Four schools with a head-coaching vacancy. USC's Daunting Schedule The good news for USC is that its remaining schedule is on the lighter side. Wait, actually, it is NOT on the lighter side! USC hosts the No. 2-ranked Ohio State Buckeyes on Saturday night. Following a bye, the Trojans will have a road matchup against the No. 4-ranked Indiana Hoosiers. They then host the Maryland Terrapins and close out the regular season with a road tilt against the archival and No. 7-ranked UCLA Bruins.

articles.title: High school soccer ref reportedly sustains broken ribs, collapsed lung after player tackles him
articles.summary: The ref is reportedly "doing better" after a visit to the hospital.
articles.body:
A high school soccer ref in Ohio reportedly sustained broken ribs and a collapsed lung after he was tackled by a player during a game, according to TMZ. The incident occurred moments after the ref gave the player's teammate a red card.

Footage of the penalty, and the hit, were captured during the contest, which took place Tuesday during a game between Steubenville High School and New Philadelphia High School.

In the clip, a player from Steubenville can be seen running toward and possibly saying something to the ref after a stoppage in play. The ref quickly pulls out a red card, prompting a different player from Steubenville to run across the field and body-check the ref to the ground.

The ref laid on the ground for the rest of the clip. One Steubenville player corralled the teammate who hit the ref. Multiple members of the Steubenville team can be spotted bringing their hands to their face in shock following the incident.

The player who tackled the ref was ejected from the contest, which New Philadelphia won 2-1.

On Wednesday, both Steubenville High School and the Ohio High School Athletic Association (OHSAA) released statements addressing the matter, per WTOV9 in Ohio.

Steubenville City Schools Superintendent Melinda Young said discipline has been imposed, though the district is not allowed to discuss it due to " student privacy laws ." Young said Steubenville High School worked collaboratively with the OHSAA on that punishment.

The OHSAA said it agreed with the punishment, which it said was "significant." The organization used the rest of its statement to condemn physical violence against officials.

The school has indicated that punishment will be significant, which the OHSAA agrees with. Physical violence against an official is among the most serious offenses that a coach, player or fan can commit and the OHSAA will pursue this to the fullest extent possible.

The official was taken to the hospital after the incident, where he was reportedly diagnosed with broken ribs and a collapsed lung. Despite that, the official is reportedly " doing better, " per TMZ.
