articles.title: Atlanta holds off furious Golden State comeback to force Game 7 in WNBA Finals
articles.summary: The WNBA Finals are headed to a decisive Game 7 on Saturday night after the Atlanta Dream’s convincing victory over the Golden State Valkyries on Thursday.
articles.body: The WNBA Finals are headed to a decisive Game 7 on Saturday night after the Atlanta Dream’s convincing victory over the Golden State Valkyries on Thursday. The Dream dominated the Valkyries from the very jump of Game 6, building the biggest first-quarter lead in WNBA Finals history and controlling things for much of the rest of the game, though things got a bit hairy as Golden State rallied in the fourth quarter. The game finished 80-69 in favor of Atlanta. Allisha Gray led the way for Atlanta with 23 points, including the dagger 3-pointer with about a minute to go that put Game 6 on ice. Rhyne Howard added 23 and Angel Reese had yet another double-double with 15 points and 14 rebounds. The game tipped off to a loud crowd inside State Farm Arena, which was reportedly a sellout despite the tip-off happening a tick after 12:40 p.m. ET. The game had to be scheduled at the midday slot to ensure the Dream hosted a Finals game at Atlanta’s premier basketball venue rather than their typical home arena outside the city that seats around 3,500. CNN’s Coy Wire caught up with a couple of Dream fans who made sure they were at the pivotal game instead of being stuck at the office. “I had work today, but I took paid time off so they let me go,” Nyla James said. Her friend Nailah Perry, also decked out in ATL gear, said she told her boss that “something came up” and that it was a “one-in-a-million” chance to support the team she loves, so she had to be at State Farm Arena. The early tip didn’t dampen the typical home-crowd energy level these teams play in front of. “It is so loud in here. You can’t hear anything,” James told Wire. “Everybody came out to support the Dream. It is so amazing!” The drama over where Game 6 would be played was quickly forgotten as the Dream started fast. A 13-0 run in the first quarter helped the Dream jump out to a double-digit lead in the opening minutes with Allisha Gray leading the way with eight points in the first seven minutes. By the end of the first quarter, the lead had grown to 17 – the largest first-quarter lead in Finals history – on the back of the Dream’s 11-15 shooting, six of which were from 3-point range. The lead grew in the second quarter as the Valkyries couldn’t quite find their shooting form, going 9-34 from the floor in the half. The lead reached 25 at one point in the quarter, but Golden State made a run in the final minutes to make it 46-26 at halftime in favor of the Dream. The tide did not turn after the halftime break as the Dream continued to dominate, and the game started to get chippy. Howard went up for a layup on a fast break and was on the receiving end of a hard foul by Veronica Burton, with the Golden State player knocking Howard to the ground after a blow to the face. Burton was whistled for a flagrant foul and the ensuing free throws rebuilt the Dream’s lead to 25. By the end of the third quarter, the Valkyries had cut the Dream’s lead to 16 points with 10 minutes to go in the game. As the heat started to turn up on the Dream in the fourth quarter with the Valkyries drawing within 13 at one point, a couple of big 3-point shots helped stymie the Golden State rally. Gray and Angel Reese nailed shots from long range on successive possessions to rebuild the Dream’s lead to 19, bringing State Farm Arena to its collective feet. But that wasn’t enough to fully put away the Valkyries, who narrowed the lead to 12 with under three minutes to go. As the game entered the final two minutes, Golden State ratcheted up the pressure. Gabby Williams’ fast-break layup fell and she was fouled in the process, leading to a free throw that brought the Dream’s lead to eight. Williams’ second-half surge was instrumental in making the game close after a quiet first half. The Dream rebuilt the lead to 11 after Gray’s corner 3-pointer dropped with about a minute to go, and then Atlanta got a crucial stop on the next possession. The Valkyries decided to allow the clock to run down and the Dream could exhale. Game 7 will be held at 8 p.m. ET on Saturday at the Chase Center in San Francisco.

articles.title: One thing Will Muschamp’s Texas defense is doing at a high level
articles.summary: The Longhorns aren’t allowing easy-access throws to opposing offenses.
articles.body:
After five seasons of it, Steve Sarkisian was fed up.

The Texas Longhorns head coach was tired of standing on the sideline and watching Pete Kwiatkowski's defense regularly give up easy-access throws, the type of completions that build confidence in quarterbacks and allow offenses to sustain drives.

So last December, Sarkisian unexpectedly fired Kwiatkowski and brought in renowned defensive coordinator Will Muschamp, his original target after leaving Tuscaloosa for Austin in early 2021.

"I felt like if you look back at us historically defensively, I felt like we were giving up too much of that, and in knowing Will and studying Will from afar, that is one of the calling cards of his defense is making sure that there are no gimmies," Sarkisian said Thursday.

With Texas fielding the No. 7 defense in ESPN's SP+ rankings, the move has paid off — even though Muschamp hadn't been a primary defensive play caller in a decade when Sarkisian hired him, Muschamp still has it.

Beyond the game-planning excellence on display in Saturday's win over Ole Miss despite the absence of star edge rusher Colin Simmons, Muschamp's defense has exactly what Sarkisian wanted in limiting the easy-access throws for opposing quarterbacks.

Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss is still completing 63.7 percent of his passes, but that number dropped significantly after the Horns held him to a career-low completion percentage of 48.1.

Sticky coverage from Texas, including the linebackers, resulted in a career-high three interceptions thrown by Chambliss, matching his entire total last year on 445 pass attempts, six batted passes, tying his season total entering the game, and four throwaways, also matching his season total entering the game.

"We made it hard and we can make it hard on people," Sarkisian said.

To accomplish that task, the Longhorns didn't just have to play tight coverage on the outside, they also had to push the pocket into the face of the quarterback generously listed at 6'0 and maintain pass-rush lane integrity to keep him from punishing the defense with scrambles or plays downfield outside the pocket.

Texas also stopped the run to make Ole Miss one-dimensional, limiting star running back Kewan Lacy to 36 yards on 16 carries. Backup Mekhi Frazier was able to break a 34-yard run, but his other five carries only went for 13 yards.

"It all ties together when you want to play that type of tight coverage," Sarkisian said.

For the first time in years, the Longhorns are tying it all together, and it's making opposing offenses earn everything they get the hard way.

articles.title: Kimi Antonelli backed to surpass Sebastian Vettel's four F1 titles by Guenther Steiner
articles.summary: Former Haas team principal Guenther Steiner has backed Kimi Antonelli to surpass Sebastian Vettel's four Formula 1 world titles
articles.body:
Former Haas Formula 1 team principal Guenther Steiner believes Kimi Antonelli will go on to have a more successful F1 career than four-time champion Sebastian Vettel .

Antonelli is on the verge of winning his maiden F1 championship, and will be crowned at this weekend's Mexican Grand Prix if he finishes in the top nine. At 20, he would break Vettel's record as F1's youngest champion, set in 2010.

Vettel went on to win four consecutive titles with Red Bull between 2010 and 2013.

Steiner discussed Antonelli's future during an appearance on The Red Flags Podcast .

"Absolutely," Steiner said when asked whether he thinks Antonelli will become more successful than Vettel. "I mean Vettel was good, but I mean Vettel was also at the right time, at the right place. But if you see when he went to Ferrari , there was not a lot left. Sebastian was very good, but he was not an exceptional talent like Max [Verstappen], or I think Kimi will be."

Asked to clarify if he thinks Antonelli will win more than four championships, Steiner confirmed: "Yes."

In just his second season in F1, Antonelli took the lead of the drivers' championship after back-to-back wins at the Chinese and Japanese Grands Prix. Since then, he has gone on to claim nine grand prix wins in total.

He currently leads the standings with 365 points, ahead of his Mercedes team-mate George Russell in second on 242 points. Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton follows in third on 241 points.

"The championships are moving closer, but our mindset does not change. Thinking about the outcome won't help us achieve it," Mercedes team chief Toto Wolff said in the Brackley outfit's Mexican Grand Prix preview.

"We will stay disciplined, take each session as it comes, and concentrate on doing the fundamentals well."

While Antonelli could claim the drivers' championship this weekend, Mercedes also has the opportunity to secure the constructors' title. Mercedes leads on 607 points after the United States Grand Prix, 133 points clear of Ferrari on 474.

articles.title: Colts sign OT Charlie Heck to 53-man roster
articles.summary: The Colts traded guard Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks this week and they filled the opening that move created on their roster on Thursday.
articles.body:
The Colts traded guard Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks this week and they filled the opening that move created on their roster on Thursday.

They announced that they have signed free agent offensive tackle Charlie Heck to their 53-man roster.

Heck was a 2020 fourth-round pick by the Texans and he spent four years in Houston before moving on to stints with the Cardinals, 49ers and Buccaneers. He went to camp with the Dolphins this summer, but failed to make the team.

Heck made 21 starts with the Texans and has started 29 of the 67 games he's played in over the course of his career.

articles.title: Who would replace Charles Leclerc at Ferrari if he misses a race for his baby’s birth?
articles.summary: With Charles Leclerc potentially facing a clash between his Formula 1 commitments and the birth of his baby, attention turns to Ferrari's reserve
articles.body:
Charles Leclerc insists he will not miss a grand prix when his first child is born, but Ferrari has reportedly lined up a stand-in in case plans change.

The Monegasque and his wife Alexandra are expecting their first baby during the last weeks of the 2026 Formula 1 season. The couple have not revealed when the baby is expected, but Alexandra's last F1 appearance was at the Madring in September which gives us a little to go on.

With five long-haul races still to come, starting in Mexico City this weekend, Leclerc will be finishing the season with a hectic stint of flights.

"I don't think I'll miss a race, but obviously I'll do absolutely everything to be at home as much as possible in between those races," Leclerc said in Austin. "So, I might arrive a little bit late. But I will be doing the races on Sunday."

So who would Ferrari call on if he could not make it?

It's understood that Ferrari Driver Academy member Dino Beganovic is the most likely driver to stand in for Leclerc and be partner to Lewis Hamilton .

The 22-year-old Swede is competing in Formula 2 this year, but already has some experience of this year's Ferrari after he drove Hamilton's car in first practice in Barcelona earlier this season. He also took part in a second FP1 session in Leclerc's car in Austria.

He is due to become Ferrari's official reserve, test and development driver in 2027.

Ferrari's long-serving reserve driver Antonio Giovinazzi is another option. The Italian raced in F1 with Alfa Romeo between 2019 and 2021, and has since driven for Ferrari in the World Endurance Championship.

He's not expected to be first in line to the Scuderia throne, and to make things harder for him, he will be unavailable during the weekend of the Brazilian Grand Prix anyway due to his responsibilities in the WEC.

#51 Ferrari AF Corse Ferrari 499P: Antonio Giovinazzi

Ferrari junior Ollie Bearman will already be behind the wheel of a Haas F1 car, while fellow academy driver Rafael Camara has not yet driven in an F1 session, making both highly unlikely choices.

Leclerc is fifth in the drivers' championship, and Ferrari is second in the constructors' standings, 133 points behind Mercedes ahead of this weekend. The Italian team is well clear of Red Bull and McLaren , which are tied for third, so missing a single race would be unlikely to cost it second place.

Leclerc has finished second in each of the last two races, in Singapore and Austin, and said after the US Grand Prix that he was confident of having "a shot to win a race before the end of the season".

articles.title: Warriors Fans Float Trade Scenarios for Pelicans Duo as Steph Curry Title Window Could Get Major Boost Amid Latest Report
articles.summary: It’s clear that if the Golden State Warriors want to maximize Stephen Curry’s title window, they need to improve their defensive firepower, as that remains o...
articles.body:
It's clear that if the Golden State Warriors want to maximize Stephen Curry's title window, they need to improve their defensive firepower, as that remains one of their weaknesses.

According to In The N.O.'s Shamit Dua , sources say the Warriors have inquired about trading for New Orleans Pelicans center Yves Missi as they look to add more frontcourt depth.

Missi, a third-year player, could be an intriguing addition. However, to acquire him, Golden State would need to make the salaries work and give up assets that would make the deal worthwhile for New Orleans.

Dua also pointed out that the Pelicans are open to trading Herb Jones, who has been on the Warriors' radar for quite some time. New Orleans is reportedly asking for two first-round picks in return for Jones.

With Porziņģis reportedly contemplating his future amid ongoing health concerns, Warriors fans have floated trade proposals involving his contract as Golden State looks to improve its forward rotation and frontcourt depth if it hopes to make the playoffs and potentially put together another championship run as it did in 2022.

With that in mind, here are some of the trade scenarios fans have come up with that could entice the Pelicans.

"Would y'all do this? Warriors get: Herb Jones Yves Missi Pelicans get: Kristaps Porzingis Two first-round picks," one fan posted this proposed trade on X.

Two first-round picks," one fan posted this proposed trade on X.

If the Warriors were to acquire both Jones and Missi, the deal could involve moving Porzingis' $20 million contract while taking on Jones' $14.9 million salary and Missi's $3.5 million deal.

However, given Golden State's cap situation, the Warriors would likely have to give up more than just Porzingis and draft picks to entice the rebuilding Pelicans. They may need to include a couple of additional players alongside their draft capital to make the deal work.

The Warriors have made no secret of their desire to add to their roster rather than subtract from it. With significant cap flexibility and an arsenal of draft capital, they're in a strong position to make good on those ambitions.

Warriors' slow start to the season shows they need to make some moves

To briefly recap, Golden State began its season on a dismal three-game losing streak, barely looking like a playoff team and getting handily outplayed in the majority of those games.

Though the Warriors snapped their slump with back-to-back wins behind Steph Curry and rookie Yaxel Lendeborg's impressive performances, it also showed that the team still isn't fully equipped for a deep playoff run. Though it is still very early in the season, Golden State needs more depth to compete with the league's top teams in the postseason.

With the season still in its early stages, the Warriors appear prepared to listen to offers and make strategic moves to improve their roster and make a push for a deep postseason run.

articles.title: Report: Bears release DE Jamree Kromah
articles.summary: The Bears are set to release Jamree Kromah to make room for Jeffery Simmons.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears need to open up a roster spot for All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, and it looks like one of their preseason standouts is the casualty. According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz, the Bears are releasing defensive end Jamree Kromah to make room for Simmons.

Kromah entered the league as an undrafted free agent in 2024 out of James Madison but was waived following roster cuts at the end of the preseason. Following a stint with the New England Patriots, Kromah returned to Chicago in 2025 as a practice squad player. In 2026, however, Kromah impressed enough throughout training camp and the preseason to earn a spot on the active roster. He appeared in two games and notched two tackles, including one for a loss.

The projected move comes hours after multiple reports of the Bears landing Simmons, along with a 2028 fifth-round pick from the Tennessee Titans in exchange for first-round picks in 2027 and 2028, and a fourth-round pick in 2027. Simmons instantly transforms the Bears' defense and gives them a bona fide star on their defensive line.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham dishes on what Brittney Griner is really like
articles.summary: Sophie Cunningham and 10-time WNBA All-Star Brittney Griner were teammates on the Phoenix Mercury from 2019 to 2024. Griner has become an easy target and has...
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham and 10-time WNBA All-Star Brittney Griner were teammates on the Phoenix Mercury from 2019 to 2024. Griner has become an easy target and has no shortage of critics, but Cunningham certainly isn't one of them.

"Brittney Griner gets the worst rap. She is the coolest person you will ever meet, swear to God. She's down to earth, she's country, just chill. She's the best," Cunningham said in a recent appearance on Theo Von's podcast.

The only criticism Cunningham had surrounding Griner was aimed not at her former teammate, but rather at Griner's security detail.

"There was one guy who was kind of our security. He was carrying her Louis Vuitton bags, and when he ran to push people away, he threw the bags, and it came back and cracked me right in the nose," Cunningham said.

"I was like, 'Da*n, I was trying to help, but I just get cracked by a $5,000 bag right in my schnoz.' Black eye the next day. It was great."

This isn't the first time it's become apparent that Griner and Cunningham are good friends. Political commentator Riley Gaines noted as much back in September whle attending a game in which the two faced each other.

"I think most people would have thought that Sophie and Brittney Griner wouldn't like each other. Kind of cool because I watched Brittney Griner and Sophie Cunningham like really embrace each other and have kind of like an intimate moment where clearly words were exchanged," Gaines said .

The two may even end up being teammates again. After the Indiana Fever's season ended, then-general manager Amber Cox said that the team would work with Cunningham on bringing her back in free agency. However, Cox was fired last week, and Cunningham has admitted that there wasn't a lot of warning that the change was coming, and that she'd have to see what happens next.

"There was not a lot of warning and that's OK," she said in a clip shared on X . "I think that's probably a good thing that you kind of keep it in-house a little bit."

"Hopefully the Fever come in and bring people who can do a really good job for that program," she added. "I was blessed to be under Kelly and Amber and I hope them the very best. So, we'll see what happens."

articles.title: Red Wings' Dylan Larkin to sit out as he awaits trade: 'Dylan's had enough of the situation'
articles.summary: Larkin requested a trade in June and has reportedly expanded his trade list to 10 teams.
articles.body:
Dylan Larkin will be held out of the Detroit Red Wings' lineup as he awaits a trade from the only NHL franchise's he's known. Beginning with Thursday's night's game against the Chicago Blackhawks, the forward will sit for trade-related reasons.

"Dylan's had enough of the situation," said Larkin's agent, Pat Brisson, in a statement. "We believe he's been very professional and cooperative through this process."

Interim general manager Shawn Horcoff is expected to address the situation on Thursday.

After requesting a trade in the summer, the 30-year-old Larkin reported to training camp in September ready to play as Horcoff continued working on a move. The team stripped Larkin of his captaincy and the forward has since been booed during the home opener and subsequent games at Little Caesars Arena.

During a press conference last month, Larkin did not elaborate on why he wants a trade out of Detroit, only saying he does not regret the decision.

"It wasn't easy to get to that decision. It was very hard. It wasn't a spur-of-the-moment thing," Larkin said . "But I don't take what I did lightly, and I got to that point, and I'm not quite ready to talk about it."

Hindering Horcoff and former general manager Steve Yzerman in the pursuit of a speedy trade is Larkin's contract, which features a full no-trade clause. When the request was made in June, Yzerman, who stepped down from the position in July , said Larkin's agent provided a "short list" of teams his client would be open to waiving his no-trade clause to join.

Larkin, who is in the the fifth season of an eight-year, $69.9 million contract extension, has reportedly expanded his trade list to 10 teams in order to help facilitate a move.

A Michigan native, Larkin was drafted by the Red Wings 15th overall in 2014 out of the University of Michigan. He has played in 10 of Detroit's 12 games this season, missing two due to injury and recorded two goals and six points.

Simon Edvinsson situation still unresolved

Larkin isn't the only situation where Horcoff needs to find a resolution. Defenseman Simon Edvinsson is a restricted free agent and has yet to be re-signed. The 23-year-old has not requested a move like Larkin, but has until Dec. 1 to sign a contract otherwise he will be ineligible to play for the rest of the 2026-27 season.

Edvinsson was drafted sixth overall by the Red Wings in 2021 and has 19 goals and 60 points in 175 career games.

articles.title: Andre Cojoe 'has real sense of confidence' ahead of first career start for Texas football
articles.summary: Texas football coach Steve Sarkisian says week of practice will help Andre Cojoe, who's replacing All-American Trevor Goosby at left tackle
articles.body:
For a few moments after All-American left tackle Trevor Goosby went down with a knee injury in last week's win over Ole Miss , things looked dire for Texas football .

Backup Andre Cojoe entered the game and immediately gave up a strip sack to Rebel edge rusher Blake Purchase. Teammate Kam Franklin recovered the fumble by Texas quarterback Arch Manning for a defensive touchdown.

But the play oddly seemed to settle Cojoe down. The 6-foot-6, 340-pound senior from Timberview High School outside of Fort Worth held his own in pass protection the rest of the game and created plenty of push in the run game.

Better yet, Cojoe has looked even stronger after a full week of practice with the first team, Texas coach Steve Sarkisian said Thursday during his weekly Zoom call with reporters.

"I feel good about (him)," Sarkisian said. "I think he should have a real sense of confidence. Was he perfect last week? No, but I think there was plenty from last week's game that he can build off of."

Andre Cojoe likely to replace Trevor Goosby

Cojoe has experience at Texas (5-2, 2-2 SEC) even though he missed all of last season with a knee injury. He appeared in four games as a sophomore in 2024 and was challenging Brandon Baker for the starting spot at right tackle prior to the 2025 season before tearing a knee ligament .

This year, Cojoe appeared in six games as a reserve before filling in for Goosby against Ole Miss. Saturday's game against Mississippi State will mark his first career start.

But even with that experience, it's hard to replicate the workload it takes to start for Texas, said his coach.

"It's human nature, right?" Sarkisian said. "I mean, we can say all day long that you've got to prepare like you're the starter. You got to prepare like you're going to be in on the second play of any series, and that's for any backup at any position.

"And then you actually get thrown in there, and then it's the physical grind of playing 50, 60, 70 snaps, but it's also the mental grind of it. I think having a week of preparation allows him to prepare for that physical and mental grind, the nuances of the plan, the communication with the guards."

Tight end Michael Masunas acknowledges the challenges of replacing someone like Goosby, who bypassed an opportunity to enter the 2026 NFL Draft after drawing first-round grades from the scouts. But Mansunas, a senior transfer from Michigan State, also understands the grueling nature of the game. Injuries create opportunities, and the game moves on regardless of who takes the field.

"It's a tough loss, but Cojoe's there working in," Masunas said Monday. "It's a sad thing to say, but next man up. That's kind of how football is nowadays. It's next guy up, and it's going to be great to see what Cojoe is able to do with the full week of practice with the ones. I think he's going to be doing great."

articles.title: 2026-27 Big East preview: The bottom of the conference
articles.summary: The bottom of the Big East is stronger than in the past.
articles.body:
UConn men's basketball is the preseason favorite to win the Big East this season, with the Huskies earning the top spot in the preseason coaches' poll . With the regular season just days away, it's time to take a look at the entirety of the Big East, starting from the bottom and working to the top. Teams are in order of their ranking in the Big East coaches' poll, with this preview focusing on the bottom of the conference — No. 9 Seton Hall, No. 10 Georgetown and No. 11 Butler. Each team's respective preseason KenPom rankings are in parentheses.

Pirates head coach Shaheen Holloway is arguably one of the top coaches in the conference, but Seton Hall's lack of funding prevents Holloway from doing much more than trying to turn water into wine. That lack of support expedited Na'jai Hines' transfer from SHU to UConn, but Holloway found an admirable fill in with Devin Williams, who was one of the best shot blockers in the country last season with Florida Atlantic.

Holloway replenished this roster with nine transfers, including some Power 5 guys like Simeon Wilcher from Texas and Mihailo Petrovic from Illinois. The Pirates' starting five figures to be all transfers, and it will be up to Holloway to mold it together.

Regardless of what happens, this Pirates team will be relentless on the defensive end. If Holloway can squeeze some more offensive production out of Williams, Wilcher and Radford transfer Del Jones, this team will be better than the preseason ranking pegs them to be. If one team in this tier greatly outperforms expectations, it will be the Pirates.

Projected starting lineup: Jones, Wilcher, Roddie Anderson, Elijah Fisher, Terry Copeland Jr.

Seton Hall at UConn – Wednesday, Feb. 17

This was a real quote from Hoyas head coach Ed Cooley — one of the highest-paid coaches in the conference — last season as Georgetown went on to a 16-18 record:

The Hoyas will likely be blessed with another mediocre season under Cooley. Georgetown did put together a strong backcourt in the transfer portal with the additions of Jaland Lowe (Kentucky), Elmarko Jackson (Kansas) and Vyctorius Miller (Okalahoma State), but none of those players earned preseason All-Big East honors. Depth is likely to be a problem, but big man Vince Iwuchukwu being ruled eligible is a big win for Cooley and the Hoyas. Chol Machot, a 7-footer who ranked No. 3 in block rate last season with Charleston, is long but thin and figures to be a key bench piece now that Iwuchukwu can play.

Projected starting lineup: Lowe, Miller, Iwuchukwu, Josiah Parker, Kayvaun Mulready

Georgetown at UConn – Wednesday, Dec. 23

The return of Thad Matta did not go as expected, with the Bulldogs going over .500 in just one of four seasons with Matta at the helm. That lack of success combined with a lack of resources led to Ronald Nored taking over the reins. Nored was key role player in Butler's legendary 2010 and 2011 Final Four squads, and the hope is that a younger (and cheaper) coach will allow the Bulldogs to return to glory.

Jalen Jackson is back for one last ride after averaging 9.5 points per game last season before his season was cut short with an ankle injury. Eduardo Klafke is a talented shooter (42.6 percent from three) from Ole Miss who can't do much else. North Dakota State transfer Treyson Anderson was an impactful player in the Summit League who struggled against high-major teams. Jordan Ellerbee from Florida Gulf Coast figures to be a key piece after averaging 13.1 points per game last season. It's fair not to expect much from Nored and Butler this year, but there is some experience and size up and down the roster. If Nored can coach this team up, the Bulldogs may be able to avoid last in the Big East.'

Projected starting lineup: Jackson, Anderson, Klafke, Drayton Jones, Asim Djulovic

If the Red Wings follow through, the dispute between Larkin and the organization will have escalated from an unresolved trade request into a potentially costly contract standoff.

Red Wings Expected to Suspend Dylan Larkin

Khan also indicated that a statement from interim general manager Shawn Horcoff was still pending.

The distinction is important: Detroit has not officially announced a suspension , and Horcoff has not yet publicly explained how the organization intends to handle Larkin's refusal to play.

Larkin was ruled out against the Chicago Blackhawks after missing Wednesday's practice and Thursday's optional morning skate.

articles.title: Titans players react to Jeffery Simmons trade: 'Obviously hurts'
articles.summary: Titans players reacted with shock and surprise after learning the team had traded defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears on Oct. 29.
articles.body:
A day after Jeffery Simmons addressed reporters about his desire to be a Tennessee Titan, his locker room seat was empty. It was a far cry from his belief that he wasn't going to be traded .

"I haven't heard from my agent, anything from this organization," Simmons told reporters before practice Oct. 28. "As far as I know, I'm going to be here ."

By the morning of Oct. 29, the four-time Pro Bowl selection and 2025 First-Team All-Pro no longer had use for that jersey. He's not going to be here. He was traded to the Chicago Bears earlier that morning, a move that spread "shock" and "surprise" throughout the Titans locker room.

Jeffery Simmons, Tennessee Titans defensive lineman in NFL

"Definitely was surprised and shocked," said Titans safety Amani Hooker, who, like Simmons, was drafted by Tennessee in 2019 and spent his whole career playing with him. "I've been with Jeff ... The last game of my college career was the Outback Bowl versus Mississippi State. Then we trained for the combine together, then got drafted together.

"Great friend. Hell of a player. Obviously hurts."

What John Franklin-Myers said about Titans trading Jeffery Simmons to Bears

The Titans' plan when they signed John Franklin-Myers to a three-year deal in March 2026 was for him Jeffery Simmons to form a disruptive duo on the defensive line.

Thanks to some injuries to the former, that never really panned out.

"We didn't (talk)," Franklin-Myers said of he and Simmons after the trade. "Truthfully, it happened so fast, (expletive), life goes on.

Inside Titans vs Browns. Cam Ward, Jeffery Simmons and our best photos

"The sad part of the business is we all wish we could've spent the next three hours with him and hugged and whatever. It don't matter. Life goes on. You've got to continue to build. Practice starts in 15 minutes. We're going to go out there and compete and get better and that's the name of the game."

What JC Latham said about Titans trade of Jeffery Simmons to Bears

Titans offensive lineman JC Latham, like his teammates, was surprised to hear Simmons had been traded.

"He was a great leader," Latham said. "You really saw the pain on his face this morning when the news broke. We took a brief second, as a team, just to say whatever we had to say, get it off our chest.

"That's when you could see how much this team meant to him, and how much the city meant to him. ... He's grown here. He's become an icon here. He's become a pillar of the community, a leader, the best player at his position. He means so much not only to the team, but the city of Nashville and the whole state of Tennessee."

articles.title: Brock Faber Clears Protocol; MN Wild Lose Spurgeon a Bit Longer
articles.summary: One of the Minnesota Wild's top defensemen took a big step forward Thursday, while another is now week to week.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Wild host the New York Islanders tonight at 7 p.m. CDT. They sit first in the Central Division at 9-3-2. And they have done it all without one of their top defensemen, local hockey legend, Brock Faber.

The former Gopher out of Maple Grove has yet to play a game this season. His last time on the ice was the Wild's final preseason game against the Dallas Stars (Sept. 25). Faber's night ended in between the second and third periods, after he was hit in the earhole by a puck that fractured his skull .

Brock Faber cleared to start skating soon

He played with the "scary" injury for the remainder of the second period, before he was finally removed. The 24-year-old underwent surgery two days later. Thankfully, head coach John Hynes gave the most positive update on Faber, to date, almost with a flurry of other injury updates and roster moves.

Hynes told gathered media today that Faber has been cleared in his return-to-play protocol, though there is no timetable for his return yet. Also notable: He can start skating in a few days.

Hynes: Fabes is cleared to return, not to play but in protocol to play: Exercise, workouts, he will start skating in a day or so. I don't have a timetable yet, maybe in a couple of days. Foligno bro's & Gus are also skating. Gus should return to practising in roughly 2 weeks. — Amwa (@Atothetease) October 29, 2026

Hynes: Fabes is cleared to return, not to play but in protocol to play: Exercise, workouts, he will start skating in a day or so. I don't have a timetable yet, maybe in a couple of days. Foligno bro's & Gus are also skating. Gus should return to practising in roughly 2 weeks.

Last season, Faber had 15 goals and 51 points in 80 games while averaging 24:41 of ice time. In the playoffs, he went off for four goals and 10 points in 11 games, averaging an incredible 29:44 of ice time.

Given the injuries Minnesota has been dealing with on the blue line since Faber went out of the lineup, the timing of his step forward couldn't be much better.

Jared Spurgeon week to week; Lambos recalled

Speaking of, we got an update on captain Jared Spurgeon Thursday too. Unfortunately, it wasn't nearly as positive. His upper body injury has now been moved from day-to-day to week-to-week.

Spurgeon returned to the Wild lineup on Oct. 22 , after missing four games with an upper-body injury. Before that injury, the 36-year-old had five points in six games and was averaging 22:22 a night.

In response, the Wild recalled defenseman Carson Lambos from AHL Iowa on Thursday, to add some depth on the blue line. Lambos, 23, has one goal and one assist in eight games with Iowa this season.

articles.title: Seahawks plan to start Quenton Nelson at left guard Monday night
articles.summary: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald confirmed that the team won't be changing Quenton Nelson's position when he takes the field with the team for the first ti...
articles.body:
Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald confirmed that the team won't be changing Quenton Nelson's position when he takes the field with the team for the first time.

Nelson played left guard throughout his time with the Colts and Macdonald said at a Thursday press conference that Nelson will remain at that spot in Seattle. Grey Zabel has been the starter at that spot, but he will switch to the right side and Anthony Bradford will move into a reserve role.

Macdonald also confirmed that the Seahawks plan to have Nelson taking his first game snaps with the team against the Bears on Monday night.

Nelson could be matched up with a familiar foe in his Seahawks debut. The Bears traded for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons on Thursday and the two players met a number of times while they were playing in the AFC South, including the Titans' upset win over the Colts a couple of weeks ago.

articles.title: Ravens reveal uniform combination for Week 8 showdown vs. Bills
articles.summary: The Ravens will wear their primary black helmets, white jerseys, white pants and white socks for Sunday's Week 8 matchup against Buffalo
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens will return to a familiar road look for Sunday's Week 8 showdown against the Buffalo Bills , wearing a white-on-white uniform combination at Highmark Stadium. Baltimore announced Thursday that it will wear its primary black helmet, white jersey, white pants, and white socks when it faces Buffalo at 1 p.m. ET.

The combination features the team's traditional black helmet with the Ravens logo, paired with white jerseys and matching pants. The look is part of Baltimore's redesigned uniform collection, introduced in 2026 as the franchise celebrates its 30th season.

The updated white jerseys feature Baltimore across the chest, with purple numerals and the team's redesigned sleeve details. The white pants feature purple striping inspired by a raven's talons, while the collection incorporates iridescent accents that reflect the franchise's traditional colors.

The Ravens have emphasized the connection to the city throughout their new uniform collection, titled "The Next Flight," which includes updated typography, helmet designs, and details inspired by Baltimore's history. Baltimore Ravens – baltimoreravens.com

Sunday's combination will contrast with Buffalo's primary blue home uniforms. The Bills enter Week 8 at 5-1 after their bye week, while Baltimore tries to end a two-game losing streak. ColorWay Sports

The Ravens wore purple jerseys and purple pants during last week's 35-13 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals, making Sunday's white-on-white combination another change in their weekly uniform rotation. Baltimore enters the matchup at 4-3 following consecutive AFC North losses to Cleveland and Cincinnati. The Ravens could receive a significant boost from quarterback Lamar Jackson, who returned to practice this week after missing three consecutive games with an ankle injury.

With Baltimore attempting to regain momentum and improve its AFC playoff positioning, the Ravens will head to Buffalo wearing one of the franchise's most recognizable road combinations.

articles.title: Tigers backed out of a Skubal trade with Milwaukee, per report
articles.summary: Turns out, the Brewers really did come with a strong package for Skubal.
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers are now your new World Series champions. The retrospectives are already here, as Andy McCullough of The Athletic has an article out today tracing their path to the franchise's first World Series title. One note is particularly interesting for Tigers fans. According to this report, the Brewers made a very competitive offer for Tarik Skubal at the trade deadline, and the Tigers had accepted it in principle. The Brewers front office thought they might have a deal done, only to watch as Zyhir Hope was pulled from his Double-A game and a deal between the Tigers and Dodgers was announced instead.

Well, kudos to the Brewers, who clearly didn't need much help. The reported deal was for two top 100 position players in infielder Luis Pena and utility player Jett Williams, along with outfielder Josh Adamczewski. The Tigers wanted pitching, but the Brewers were unwilling to part with rookie left-hander Logan Henderson in a deal. So the offer was the best offer they were going to make when Scott Harris called to ask for their best package before moving to the Dodgers to get their final offer. Not long after, they noted the Hope news, and Harris called back to tell them he was going with a different offer.

"I appreciated the s— out of that," Arnold said. "He was very transparent." The timing allowed Milwaukee to pivot and trade for St. Louis reliever JoJo Romero and starter Dustin May. But they did not add an ace.

Instead, the Tigers accepted the deal for Zyhir Hope, who is similarly ranked to Williams, along with injured right-hander River Ryan and High-A pitching prospect Brady Smith. Smith and Adamczewski are pretty comparable, thought the latter is graded a notch higher by some prospect sites.

I'm a big fan of Luis Pena, so this pains me a little bit, but at the same time, the Brewers had to know the Tigers were hunting for pitching with both Skubal and Casey Mize headed to free agency. Someday this may be a very interesting what if, as the Brewers package was the stronger offer on paper. It just didn't address the Tigers main need, which was pitching to fill the gap until their stock of A-ball level pitching prospects develops further. It really all comes down to Ryan, and whether he can finally put the injuries behind him and reach his potential as a frontline starter or potential ace reliever.

It's an interesting little study in approach as well. Harris asked for the final best offers and picked the best package from his perspective. It's tricky balancing need vs. overall value in all sports, but particularly in baseball. Maybe if Harris had acquired both Pena and Williams, he could turn entirely to pitching in free agency with a killer group of position prospects on their way to bolster what they already have in Kevin McGonigle, Max Clark, and others. But adding pitching in free agency has not been a front office strength. As far as potentially trading Williams or someone else for cost-controlled pitching later on, the truth is that acquiring arm talent with significant team control is really difficult. No one wants to give up inexpensive pitching, even for a good position player generally ranked in the middle of many top 100 lists. Certainly not during the offseason.

We'll see how it all shakes out in the long run, but it was interesting to get a bit more of a blow-by-blow of events than has been previously reported. Good to know Harris didn't just string anyone along and potentially leave the Brewers scrambling in the final minutes. That's the kind of thing that can really put other teams off from dealing with you again, but it's certainly not mandatory to inform a team that their trade isn't accepted. They sometimes don't find out until a deal is already complete.

The report is a bit of housekeeping from a Tigers fans perspective, but we'll take it as closure on the 2026 Skubal saga. Let the offseason begin.

articles.title: Rabbit Evans’ ‘relentless effort’ that saved a touchdown
articles.summary: Each week, Morgan Scalley highlights plays that exemplify Utah’s culture. Rabbit Evans’ touchdown-saving tackle surely made the cut.
articles.body:
On third-and-5 during Houston's second drive of the game, quarterback Conner Weigman hit speedy receiver Amare Thomas in the middle of the field.

Thomas, a projected NFL draft pick, quickly turned upfield, evading Jackson Bennee and Elijah Davis for a gain of 56 yards. Just as it looked like Thomas would go the distance for an early touchdown, safety Rabbit Evans came sprinting over to make a tackle that saved six points.

The Utes were able to stand strong in the red zone, stuffing Weigman on a quarterback keeper on third-and-1 and forcing a field goal.

Evans' "relentless" effort saved four points and kept Utah's deficit manageable.

"The effort is there. They're relentless to the football. … There was a deep pass to No. 0 and Rabbit Evans runs it down," Utah coach Morgan Scalley said. "If Rabbit Evans doesn't take off once he sees that, the guy scores a touchdown."

"I mean, that's huge. You got to go back to that. You got to promote it and your guys have to see how valuable that is, that OK, that wasn't my mistake, that wasn't my guy, but I'm going to take off and I'm going to go. He makes that tackle and they don't get seven."

Each week, Scalley highlights plays that exemplify Utah's "relentless, smart, nasty, ballhawks" culture. Evans' touchdown-saving tackle surely made the cut during film review this week.

"Honestly, I was just like, 'Just go get him.' … When I came down and I took my angle, I really wasn't looking at the receiver. I just put my head down and just started running until I felt like I got close to get him," Evans said.

"But that was a huge play in that game because we ultimately stopped him in the red zone. So just that relentless effort that we play with, it continues to show up and we just got to just keep playing, just keep doing that."

In his third season at Utah after missing nearly all of last year with an injury, Evans has been one of Utah's best — and most consistent — defensive players. He's logged 30 tackles and a sack, recovered a fumble, intercepted two passes and broken up three passes.

The key to his play this year? Feeling able to play fast and free.

"I would say just recognizing the plays that's coming, just being able to play fast, play free. Our coach has given us the luxury to do that. So just continuing to play fast, play confident, really," Evans said.

As Utah enters the tough part of its schedule and plays some great offenses and quarterbacks, the Utes will need more of that "relentless" effort and high-level play from Evans.

The Utes received a deluge of praise following an impressive win over Houston, but Scalley cautioned his team not to buy into the hype.

"Beware the soothing sounds of praise," Scalley said.

articles.title: FSU quarterback embraces challenge ahead of Clemson
articles.summary: Ashton Daniels told ACC analyst Eric Mac Lain he believes he is playing his best football while outlining the challenge Clemson’s defense presents.
articles.body:
Florida State quarterback Ashton Daniels believes he is playing his best football of the season, even if he still sees plenty left on the field. During an interview with ACC analyst Eric Mac Lain, Daniels reflected on his recent play and looked ahead to Saturday night's matchup with the Clemson Tigers at Doak Campbell Stadium.

"I'm playing my best football right now, but I also know I'm leaving so much out there on the field," Daniels said. "A couple plays here and there that maybe I made the right decision, I made the right read, had a better throw, and would've put us in even better position to win the game."

That confidence comes after one of Daniels' strongest performances of the season. Against the Miami Hurricanes, he threw for 298 yards and four touchdowns while adding another score on the ground in FSU's 43-35 double-overtime loss. The performance earned Daniels his second ACC Quarterback of the Week honor of the season.

Daniels said the next step is continuing to build on that progress.

"For me now, it's just continue to stack and be better than yesterday," he said.

Clemson will provide a difficult test, particularly in the secondary. Daniels singled out junior cornerback Ashton Hampton, calling him "one of the best corners in the country." Hampton has earned Midseason All-America recognition from multiple outlets and has recorded an interception and nine pass breakups this season.

"I'm just excited for that," Daniels said. "To be able to go and prove my connection with Duce or Micahi or anybody in the receiver room against a very, very, very talented DB room."

The challenge extends beyond Clemson's secondary. The Tigers have recorded 20 sacks through seven games, third-most in the ACC, and are averaging 2.86 per game. Clemson is also allowing only 317 yards per contest, fifth-best in the conference.

"It's going to be a great challenge," Daniels said.

Florida State hosts Clemson Saturday at 7 p.m. ET on ACC Network. The Seminoles enter at 3-4, looking to snap a two-game losing streak and begin the final five-game stretch of the regular season with a win.

articles.title: Austin Siereveld’s return might matter more than anyone realizes
articles.summary: Whoever starts at quarterback against USC will need protection more than anything. Austin Siereveld’s return gives Ohio State their best offensive line back...
articles.body:
Ohio State's biggest question this week is obvious. Ryan Day still hasn't named a starting quarterback, and he said Tuesday it's "definitely possible" both Luke Fahey and Tavien St. Clair play against USC.

Whoever starts, the most important thing for that quarterback might be the return of a guy who hasn't played in almost a month.

Austin Siereveld is back at practice this week after missing Ohio State's last two games with an illness. Day said it'll be determined over the course of the week whether he's ready for a full game, but if he plays, it'll be at tackle.

That might not sound like the biggest headline of the week, but I think it could be one of the most important developments for Ohio State's offense in Los Angeles.

In my piece before the Indiana game, I wrote that if Ohio State lost in Bloomington, it would probably start at offensive tackle . The Buckeyes won, but the right side of the line was a problem all afternoon.

Without Siereveld, Phillip Daniels returned at right tackle after missing a month, and Gabe VanSickle moved back to right guard. It did not go well.

Sayin was sacked four times, two each by Mario Landino and Tobi Osunsanmi, and was under pressure all afternoon. The sack that ended his season came when Landino beat Daniels around the right side. Ohio State's run game didn't fare much better, finishing with just 78 rushing yards.

That's not all on Daniels. He was playing his first game in over a month against one of the best defensive lines in the country, and anyone would have looked rusty. But it showed how much the line misses Siereveld's steadiness on that side.

Siereveld is a team captain, and Day has called him Ohio State's best offensive lineman. He's also the most versatile.

He came into the season as the starting right guard, then slid out to right tackle when Daniels was hurt at Texas and played there for three straight games. When he was healthy, Ohio State's line looked like a real strength.

The last time he played was at Iowa on Oct. 3. That day, Ohio State's five starters, Ian Moore at left tackle, Luke Montgomery at left guard, Carson Hinzman at center, VanSickle at right guard and Siereveld at right tackle, played all 75 offensive snaps together against one of the best defenses in the country.

Ohio State put up 484 yards, and the Jacksons combined for 142 rushing yards. That might be the best this line has looked all season.

Hinzman made it clear this week how much the line has missed him.

"Talk about a freak athlete, man. Very large human being," he said. "Great communicator when it comes to the offensive line."

That last part might matter most. With a quarterback making his first career start, the line has to handle the protection calls, adjust on the fly and make sure everyone is on the same page. Having your leader and best communicator back is huge.

Day's plan to play Siereveld at tackle is the right call. It gets Ohio State back to the group that played so well against Iowa, with VanSickle at guard where he's been at his best. Daniels can still provide depth if Siereveld isn't ready for a full game, but the Iowa lineup gives Ohio State its best chance to keep their young quarterback upright.

Whether it's Fahey or St. Clair, the offense has to be simple. That means running the ball, getting it out quickly and avoiding negative plays. None of that works if the right side of the line can't hold up.

USC is a good matchup for Siereveld's return. Wisconsin sacked Jayden Maiava five times last week, but USC's own pass rush isn't on Texas or Indiana's level.

If Ohio State's line can control the line of scrimmage, it can open running lanes for Bo Jackson and Isaiah West and keep the Buckeyes out of third and long, where a freshman quarterback is most vulnerable.

There's also a bigger picture element here. The defense has carried Ohio State the last few weeks, but the offense needs to be able to sustain drives too, especially in a hostile environment at night in the Coliseum. A healthy, consistent offensive line is what gives Ohio State the best chance to do that.

Everyone will be watching the quarterback on Saturday night. But if Ohio State wins in Los Angeles, there's a good chance it'll be because the five guys in front of him finally got their best lineup back together.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Injury Impact: Jadarian Price Designated To Return, Damaging Emanuel Wilson And Zach Charbonnet
articles.summary: The latest injury update on Seattle Seahawks running back Jadarian Price and the fantasy football impact.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks have designated first-round rookie running back Jadarian Price to return from injured reserve. His 21-day practice window has been opened, and he should be returning to action from his chest injury soon.

While he will return to practice this week, that does not mean he will play in Week 8, although it is a possibility. This is a situation we will have to monitor closely. Zach Charbonnet's return also appears to be imminent.

Whether Price's first game back is this week or in the near future, we do not have high hopes for his fantasy value. The most likely outcome is that he just further muddies an already confusing backfield.

In three games this season, he rushed for just 119 yards on 28 carries and four receptions for 21 yards without scoring a single touchdown. He wasn't exactly lighting it up before he got injured. Price is going to return to an even deeper committee, which only further complicates things.

Wilson had a nice run, but it appears to be coming to an end. With Charbonnet and Price both on their way back, his days of seeing 20-plus carries per game are behind him. It's possible that he sneaks one more strong game in this week, but the time is coming to move on from him.

If you can sell high on Wilson, we suggest you do so as soon as possible. This backfield is going to be a nightmare to figure out as everyone gets healthy.

Charbonnet will fall right in with other backs. It will be interesting to see how he is used in his first game back, but we expect him to fall into a committee that splits carries, with Charbonnet handling the goal-line work. We were hoping that Charbonnet would get a few strong fantasy games in before Price was ready to return, but that no longer looks likely.

articles.title: No role handed to Dont'e Thornton for Raiders, has to 'beat somebody out'
articles.summary: If newly activated WR Dont'e Thornton wants a role in the Raiders offense, he's going to have to earn it and take it from someone else.
articles.body:
This week, the Raiders officially activated WR Dont'e Thornton for the first time this season after he had spent the five seven weeks on injured reserve.

Since the start of training camp, the Raiders offense have been preparing without Thornton. And if he wants to carve out a role with them, he's going to have to work his way up to do it.

"Well, he's got to take the spot of another guy, so he's got to go beat out somebody," Kubiak said of Thornton this week.

The 6-5, 205-pounder was supposed to be the frontrunner for the Raiders' X receiver job. This offseason, there wasn't much in the way of competition for that job, so all Thornton really needed to do was prove competent.

Even at his height, that was a tall task for Thornton, who made just ten catches last season on 30 targets. He was able to use his 4.3 speed to get open and his 6-5 stature to tower over many defenders, but it was the matter of actually catching the ball when it arrived that proved difficult.

What the team was hoping was that he was able to show improvements in that area coming into his second season. But he hasn't seen the field enough to offer any confidence. And the fact that they waited through the entire 21-day window before activating him wasn't exactly a great sign either.

The depth chart at the moment starts with Tre Tucker. Starting across from him is Jalen Nailor with Cody White and rookie Malik Benson seeing some snaps as well.

Outside of Tucker, none of this group has made themselves in invaluable part of the offense, so if Thornton wants to earn his way onto the field, he may not have to show off too much. Basically just do the job and catch the ball at somewhere north of, say, 40% of the time and that could be enough.
